entries.title: What makes ‘The Pitt’ so horrifyingly realistic? We asked the show’s makeup and prosthetic pros.
entries.content:
Just two seasons into its run, *The Pitt* has fast become one of the most celebrated television shows of the 21st century, combining the hour-to-hour intensity of *24*, the procedural probity of *ER*, and an IV drip of *Scrubs* to take the edge off the constant chaos and carnage in the emergency department at the Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center.

The series has won Emmys for Outstanding Drama, Lead Actor, and Supporting Actor and Actress, but *The Pitt* may be best known for its hyper-realistic portrayals of degloved flesh, dismemberment, electrocution, priapism, impalement, botched cosmetic injection, fecal disimpaction, cutaneous maggot infestation, and [childbirth](https://www.popsci.com/science/how-pregnancy-changes-body/).

Even anatomical pros marvel at the show’s veritable snuff-film visuals.

“It’s kind of like shadowing in the ER for a day,” says [Josh Johnson, Ph.D](https://www.uidaho.edu/people/jijohnson), director of the Doctor of Anatomical Sciences Program at the University of Idaho, on watching an episode. “Like, oh, my god—*this* is what you’re doing here? You’re literally cutting this person’s chest open and squeezing their heart for them.”

It’s a level of realism not previously seen on screen. Thanks to a unit of in-house and external effects and makeup practitioners who have advanced the craft light years with the help of new techniques and technologies that they are, in many cases, pioneering. We asked *The Pitt*’s pros as well as the heads of anatomy at two major medical schools to explain advances in the hospital horrors from which we are powerless to look away.

## How the prosthetic sausage is made

The order of operations on *The Pitt* is unlike almost any other production, according to head of makeup Myriam Arougheti, who says patients are often cast before a story is even plotted.

### 1. The cases

It all starts with writer and executive producer Dr. Joe Sachs, who sends Arougheti all of the medical interventions that will appear in an episode so she can get them modeled.

“Depending on the procedure, it can vary between two and nine weeks to build,” Arougheti says. “This is why it’s so important for Dr. Joe to give me in advance as much as possible, because they have to cast these actors ASAP to get their body lifecast so we can start building.”

### 2. Casting (actor *and* body)

A lifecast is a three-dimensional mold of an actor’s body from which the effects houses create scrupulous, lifelike arms, legs, chests… collapsible faces—Dr. Joe hasn’t been able to stump ’em yet. Once the actor playing the patient is chosen, they’re immediately sent in for cloning.

### 3. Prosthetic prognosis

Meanwhile, Arougheti and her team strategize how the procedures will be recreated. Once they think they have a plan for portraying an American flag protruding from a thorax, a lung being hand-rotated in an open chest cavity, or something as simple as a severed trachea getting mended, they place their orders with one of several special effects houses.

### 4. Sculpting

Taking the scalpel from here, the craftsfolk at studios like LA’s Autonomous F/X hammer out the methods and materials that will make the most convincing organs, appendages, and anatomical functions.

[View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/DVUMk7DEtM-/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

[A post shared by Autonomous F/X (@autonomousfx2005)](https://www.instagram.com/p/DVUMk7DEtM-/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

“It’s a whole new trick you have to figure out that you’re like, ‘What we did last time isn’t going to work this time,’” says [Autonomous F/X](https://autonomousfx.com/) CEO Jason Collins, who has worked previously on medical dramas like *House, M.D.*, *Resident*, and *Grey’s Anatomy*. “So we have to reinvent the wheel each time.”

### 5. Follow-up

Even with a vigorous ongoing back-and-forth between the teams, it would be expecting a lot to get the wheel right on the first try. So, once the builds are complete, Arougheti presents them to Dr. Joe for final approval in the rare case that something’s amiss.

“We’re in prep and I misunderstood one little element that the doctor told me,” Arougheti says of one such review. “And the way the sculpture was built, he was like, ‘Yeah, if the bone is like that, the patient’s dead,’ That’s why there’s constant communication between the effects houses, myself, and Dr. Joe.”

*Dr. Joe Sachs on the importance of prosthetic bodies on TV.*

## The 5 active ingredients that make *The Pitt* so (too?!) realistic

For decades, wound simulation—or moulage—relied on heavy layers of spirit gum, cotton, [collodion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collodion), and rigid modeling waxes. Much later came foam latex, but it all melted easily under hot studio lights and was shot for standard definition TVs that wouldn’t meet “standard” today.

But what modern technology disrupts, modern technology can un-rupt, so when high-definition imaging exposed the limitations of pre-millennial moulage, new practices and materials—some developed for entertainment, others for education—emerged to close the realism gap.

“We look at things more like magic tricks than as technological advances,” Collins says. “You’ve got your science and you’ve got your art [that] you have to combine together to fool the eye. Once we lose the art to the technology, I don’t know if we’re storytelling anymore.”

### Silicone’s supremacy

It wasn’t that long ago that moulage meant raiding the produce aisle, at least academically.

“When I was a kid, we learned in diabetes class how to give insulin injections by doing it into the skin of an orange, because that approximately was the feeling of human skin,” says [James Lipshaw](https://harvardmedsim.org/james-lipshaw/), assistant director, instructional design and media center for medical simulation at Harvard Medical School. “That was simulation in 1996.”

Today, silicone lies, plies, stretches, and jiggles like real flesh thanks to breakthroughs in just the last few years:

* In the late aughts, chemists began mixing in plasticizers, or “deadeners,” oily liquids that weaken silicone’s elasticity. This made it less rubbery and bouncy, allowing for more accurate emulation of loose skin.

* Around a decade ago, fabricators began layering that deadened silicone on materials like liquidized PVC and paraffin to match [composite human structures](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11858894/) of skin over fat over muscle. Everything on the bone now looked and behaved more true to life.

* In just the last couple of years, researchers refined manufacturing techniques that [engrave microscopic lines](https://3dprintingindustry.com/news/new-3d-printed-tissue-that-mimics-real-skin-for-medical-training-245267/) onto silicone to mimic collagen geometry, enhancing the texture and directional stretching of sim skin.

The result is “flesh” that gapes, lacerates, stitches, and amputates just like the real thing.

*Fake blood mats are more realistic and less messy than regular fake blood.*

### 3D scanning & printing

Historically, artists sculpted prosthetics entirely by hand using oil-based clay. It was time consuming, one-of-one, and while convincing for its time, imprecise.

[3D scanning and digital sculpting](https://www.popsci.com/technology/how-does-a-3d-printer-work/) software in the last decade has revolutionized this workflow, allowing artists to accurately reproduce [anatomy](https://www.popsci.com/basic-anatomy-healthcare-quiz/), tweak with impunity, and print multiple molds from digital files all in a fraction of the time.

“Looking at how things have changed since the days of *House M.D.*, where all of those things were a guess on our part,” Collins posits, “let’s say it’s a gasket in a heart. Now we can 3D-print that, know that it’s going to fit exactly into our heart, and it’s 99.9% accurate to what would be produced in the real world… That technology is within the last five years.”

The lifecast they take of each “patient” immediately after they’re chosen for the role is the same process writ human. They’ll scan the actor, print an anatomical clone, and then sculpt on that to create custom appliances like a hematoma or [heart nail](https://thepittcasebook.com/en/the-pitt/season-1/episode-3/hank-nail-cardiac-injury/).

### Drone technology

[Drones](https://www.popsci.com/category/drones/) aren’t just for imperiling commercial aircraft anymore. Adopting technology that powered the boom in whirring quadcopters the last decade, special effects pros have developed tiny, unobtrusive animatronics to mimic complex phenomena like aliens, dinosaurs, and… childbirth.

“We can now pack a lot into one or two remote controls and actually be pushing the baby out via mechanics behind the monitor or three doors down,” Collins says. “And I don’t believe the drone technology really got going until about 10 years ago. It used to be big controls that people would be flying remote control helicopters or airplanes, now it’s all condensed down essentially to the size of an iPhone.”

Don’t tell Harvard’s Lipshaw.

“Back in the old days when we ran a clinical labor and delivery course, I used to be the person who had to lube up and then reload our rocket spring–propelled baby that would come out of the delivery model,” he recalls. “You have to grease it back up, put it back in its blood sac, and get it back inside of the mannequin.”

The relatively recent crossover between [aerospace](https://www.popsci.com/technology/aerospace-innovations-2025/) robotics (UAVs) and animatronics allows SFX operators to maintain a lag-free wireless connection without interrupting the actors or cluttering the set with spring-loaded babies.

### A house of MDs

*The Pitt*’s secret sauce is a cadre of clinicians versed in trauma care who approve every procedure, implement, and anatomical outcome before cameras roll.

“They’re assigned a certain amount of episodes, so anytime we do anything—any cut, any bruise, any stitching—they are there at all times,” Arougheti says. They’re unyielding, but rather than feeling burdened by that exactitude, the crew feel a collective commitment to authenticity.

“[The consultants] really are the mothers and fathers of that authenticity,” Collins says. “With *The Pitt*, it’s not like they’re going to slather a bunch of blood on it and say, ‘Bob’s your uncle.’ It’s going to be very, very down to a science.”

### Time & money

Warner Bros. Discovery shareholder value be damned, Arougheti and her team get what they need when they need it from their HBO Max benefactors. That includes the budget and sometimes the months necessary to perfect a sculpt or build.

“They really give us what we need as far as time and budget. Things are not rushed,” says Arougheti, who is Emmy-nominated for the second year in a row, and previously won for HBO’s *Westworld*. “It all starts in the sculpture and in the amount of detail—skin lines, pores, all that happens in the sculpture. And so when you have the time to do that, you can really create something magical.”

The post [What makes ‘The Pitt’ so horrifyingly realistic? We asked the show’s makeup and prosthetic pros.](https://www.popsci.com/health/the-pitt-prosthetic-makeup-behind-the-science-doctors/) appeared first on [Popular Science](https://www.popsci.com).

entries.title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: Everything you need to know
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

Headline changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate include an all-new Siri AI assistant, major upgrades to apps including Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail and Calendar, expanded child-safety features, design refinements and performance improvements throughout the operating system.

Golden Gate continues Apple’s tradition of naming macOS releases after iconic Californian landmarks. More broadly, the update represents another step in Apple’s push to make the Mac smarter and more proactive, with greater use of Apple Intelligence across the operating system and a stronger focus on helping users complete everyday tasks more quickly.

macOS 27 is supported on all Macs powered by Apple silicon, marking the end of the road for Intel-based Macs. While Intel models won’t be eligible for the new operating system, Apple is expected to continue providing security updates for them for some time.

This hub covers everything you need to know about macOS 27 Golden Gate, including its new features, compatibility, beta releases and Apple Intelligence upgrades.

## What’s New in macOS 27 Golden Gate at a glance

![WWDC 2026 macOS Features](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/WWDC-2026-macOS-Features.png?w=1200)

Apple

Here are the top ten new features and changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate.

1. **Siri AI**: A redesigned conversational Siri that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access the web and take actions across apps.
2. **Apple Intelligence**: Systemwide proofreading, smarter writing tools, improved dictation and automatic file and folder naming.
3. **Safari upgrades**: Automatic tab grouping, webpage change alerts with Notify Me, AI-generated extensions and faster, more efficient browsing.
4. **Smarter Messages and Mail**: Personalized Smart Reply, better search and syncing, contextual suggestions and improved reliability.
5. **New Photos tools**: Spatial Reframing, image expansion with Extend, improved Clean Up, and better search and organization.
6. **More powerful built-in apps**: New features for Passwords, Calendar, Notes, Preview, Freeform, Weather, Shortcuts, and Image Playground.
7. **Expanded parental controls**: Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections.
8. **Better Mac gaming**: Game Porting Toolkit 4 promises significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games.
9. **Refined Liquid Glass design**: Better readability and consistency, adjustable transparency, cleaner Finder windows, and improved iPhone Mirroring.
10. **Faster macOS performance**: Quicker app launches, Spotlight, AirDrop and networking, plus improved external-display, Thunderbolt and Bluetooth support.

## macOS 27 release date: When will macOS 27 be available?

* September 14, 2026

macOS 27 has been in beta since it was unveiled at WWDC in June, but the official version of macOS 27 became available to install on compatible Macs on September 14.

## macOS 27 Beta – What’s new in the latest beta?

![Apple Beta](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Apple-Beta.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

Apple continues to release beta versions of macOS after the official release. The betas are of system updates, which have security patches, bug fixes, and sometimes new features that were not ready for the official release.

Beta software can still cause crashes, app compatibility problems, increased battery drain, and, in some cases, data loss. If you do install it, make a full backup first and ideally use a secondary Mac, separate volume or external SSD.

Here’s how you can [participate in the beta program](https://www.macworld.com/article/671123/how-to-install-macos-beta.html) we also recommend reading our guide to [whether you should install the latest macOS beta](https://www.macworld.com/article/671123/should-i-install-macos-beta-latest-version.html).

## Siri AI: Siri powered macOS 27 features

![Siri AI waitlist macOS 27](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/siri-AI-waitlist.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foiundry

Apple’s biggest focus in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Siri AI, a completely redesigned version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence. Rather than functioning primarily as a voice assistant, Siri is becoming a conversational AI that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access current information from the web and take actions across apps.

Siri AI behaves more like a generative-AI chatbot than the Siri of old. It can answer questions directly, understand natural follow-ups and solve problems instead of simply directing users to web searches.

### At a glance: What’s new with Siri AI?

**Conversational AI assistant**: Siri can handle open-ended questions, brainstorming, research and natural back-and-forth conversations.

**Dedicated Siri app**: A standalone Siri app keeps conversations in one place and syncs them through iCloud, allowing users to start a conversation on one Apple device and continue it on another.

**Personal context awareness**: Siri will be able to understand information in Messages, Mail, Notes, Photos, Maps and files to locate information and provide answers based on your personal data.

**Web-powered answers**: Siri can access current information from the web, making it more useful for research, learning, interview preparation and questions about recent events.

**App actions and automation**: Siri can perform tasks across apps such as Messages, Music, Reminders, Calendar and Maps using natural-language instructions.

**Spotlight integration**: Siri AI is integrated with Spotlight, allowing users to type questions and receive AI-generated answers without opening a browser or separate app.

**Visual Intelligence**: Visual Intelligence comes to the Mac for the first time, allowing Siri to understand selected images, documents, files, text and other content displayed on screen.

![macOS 27 Golden Gate Visual Intelligence](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/VisualIntelligence.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple’s Visual Intelligence initially placed Blutenburg in Denmark.

Macwelt

**Writing Tools**: Siri can generate text, rewrite drafts, summarise content and adjust wording or tone. Apple says it can also adapt writing to the way you typically communicate with particular contacts.

**Improved dictation**: Systemwide dictation gains better speech recognition along with automatic punctuation, capitalisation and formatting.

**Custom Siri voices**: Users can choose Siri’s voice and adjust characteristics such as pace and expressiveness, although some of these capabilities require newer hardware.

macOS 27 also contains a [Siri AI popover](https://www.macworld.com/article/3194935/macos-27-has-a-secret-popover-menu-for-ai-power-users.html). Selecting text can bring up a small Siri icon offering contextual actions, including Writing Tools, summaries and key points, sending messages or emails, creating calendar events, opening locations in Maps, and tracking flights or packages. The feature is not currently enabled by default and requires Apple’s FeatureFlags system to activate.

Apple also appears to be taking a relatively restrained approach to AI behaviour. [In our testing](https://www.macworld.com/article/3164693/siri-ai-is-both-impressive-and-disappointing.html), Siri avoids presenting itself as human, excessive flattery and potentially harmful responses, while generally keeping its answers straightforward.

Apple has also said Siri AI will still be labelled as a beta when it launches, so users should expect some rough edges and continued improvements after release.

Siri AI is initially available in English. Availability will vary by region. Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the European Union because of issues related to the Digital Markets Act, and it will remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory approvals. However, it will be available on [Mac and Vision Pro in the EU](https://www.macworld.com/article/3182183/constructive-siri-ai-meeting-sparks-hope-for-iphone-users-overseas.html).

## Which Macs support Siri AI?

Siri AI requires a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, but some of its most advanced capabilities have higher hardware requirements. Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model, expressive Siri voices and advanced dictation require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory. Macs that support Apple Intelligence but do not meet those requirements can still receive other Siri AI features, although the exact feature set may vary.

## Safari features coming in macOS 27

![safari notify me popup](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/safari-notify-me-popup.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Notify Me in Safari

Apple

Safari gets several Apple Intelligence-powered upgrades in macOS 27, including smarter tab organization, webpage monitoring, custom extension generation, and performance improvements.

* **Automatic Tab Topics**: Safari will automatically group related tabs by topic as you browse, helping keep research and projects organised. These groups can also be saved for later.
* **Notify Me**: Safari will be able to [monitor webpages for changes and alert you](https://www.macworld.com/article/3159801/my-fingers-already-love-this-macos-27-safari-feature.html) when something happens, such as a product coming back in stock or a price dropping, removing the need to keep refreshing pages manually.
* **Describe an Extension**: Users will be able to create custom Safari extensions simply by describing what they want. Safari will generate the extension from the text description and add it to the toolbar.
* **Faster, more efficient browsing**: Apple says Safari will use less power while improving page-loading speed, JavaScript performance, scrolling, animations and resizing of the Start Page.

![Browser Alarm macOS 27 Golden Gate](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/browseralarm.jpg?quality=50&strip=all)

Get notified.

Macwelt

## Messages and Mail features coming in macOS 27

Messages and Mail gain deeper Apple Intelligence integration in macOS 27, alongside improvements to search, syncing and everyday reliability.

### Messages

* **One-Tap Suggestions in Messages**: Messages will suggest useful actions based on the context of a conversation, such as creating a reminder or note without leaving the chat.
* **Smarter Photo Suggestions**: Messages will surface relevant photos based on people, places and keywords mentioned in a conversation.
* **Personalized Smart Reply**: Suggested replies can reflect your usual writing style and adapt depending on who you’re messaging.
* **Improved syncing**: Messages should sync more reliably across devices, while failed messages will automatically retry sending.

### Mail

* **Personalized Smart Reply**: Mail will also generate suggested responses that better match your writing style and the person you’re replying to.
* **More relevant search**: A new ranking system will prioritise the most useful search results, alongside improved search indexing.
* **Faster and more accurate**: Apple says Mail will load messages more quickly and provide more reliable unread counts.

## Photos features coming in macOS 27

Photos has new AI-powered editing and organization tools in macOS 27, making it easier to improve images, find photos and manage an iCloud library.

* **Spatial Reframing**: Photos will be able to intelligently recompose and reframe images after they’ve been taken.
* **Extend Tool**: A new Extend tool can expand an image beyond its original boundaries, filling in missing areas when changing the crop or aspect ratio.
* **Enhanced Clean Up**: Apple’s Clean Up tool will be better at removing larger unwanted objects and distractions from photos.
* **Better organisation and search**: Photos adds keywords, star ratings, improved metadata search and other tools for organising a library.
* **Faster iCloud syncing**: iCloud Photos can begin uploads more quickly, with an option to prioritise syncing when needed.

## Other new features coming to apps with macOS 27

macOS 27 also brings a wide range of smaller upgrades across Apple’s built-in apps, with a particular focus on automation, organisation, security and Apple Intelligence.

### Passwords

The Passwords app can automatically identify weak or compromised passwords and, with Apple Intelligence, visit supported websites, change the password and save the new credentials. This could remove much of the manual work involved in updating large numbers of old or leaked passwords, although questions remain over website compatibility, two-factor authentication and how consistently the feature will work. Read: [Apple finally got rid of my biggest password headache.](https://www.macworld.com/article/3160935/apple-finally-got-rid-of-my-biggest-password-headache.html)

### Image Playground

Image Playground gets a substantial AI upgrade, including the ability to create photorealistic images and make more convincing edits to existing pictures, such as changing colours, hair and other details. Apple continues to apply safeguards around real people, copyrighted characters and distinctive artistic styles.

![macOS Golden Gate Image Playground](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macos-golden-gate-image-playground.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

### Calendar

Calendar gains natural-language event creation, making it possible to describe an event rather than manually entering every detail. It can also make changes to multiple events at once.

### Preview

Preview supports more document formats, improves PDF editing and saves PDF files more quickly.

### Notes

Notes gains [drawing tools for sketching](https://www.macworld.com/article/3183430/macos-27-golden-gate-ai-features-freeform-image-playground-notes-weather.html) with a mouse or trackpad, along with digital signatures, Markdown copy-and-paste and links to sections within notes.

![macos golden gate notes drawing tools](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macos-golden-gate-notes-drawing-tools.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Notes now features a drawing tool as well as the ability to create and use digital signatures.

Foundry

### Freeform

Freeform adds drawing tools, collaborative folders and improved organisation, including the ability to sort boards into folders. Full dark-mode support also changes the appearance of the drawing canvas.

![macOS Golden Gate Freeform boards](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macOS-GOlden-Gate-Freeform-boards.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

In Freeform, boards can now be organised into folders.

Foundry

### Weather

Weather gets a clearer and more detailed forecast interface, with reorganised information tiles and enhanced 10-day forecasts showing precipitation probability and amount, as well as wind speeds throughout the day.

![macOS golden gate weather](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macOS-golden-gate-weather.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

In the Weather app, the tiles have been rearranged, and there are separate 10-day forecasts for precipitation and wind (circled in red).

Foundry

### Shortcuts

Shortcuts gains a redesigned editor, more automation capabilities and one of macOS 27’s more ambitious AI features: the ability to turn natural-language instructions into working automations.

![macOS Golden Gate automatischer Kurzbefehl](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Automatischer-Kurzbefehl.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Shortcuts can start automatically when a specific event occurs.

Thomas Armbrüster

### Parental Controls

Apple expands its family-safety tools with Safari’s Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time and Time Allowances, contact approvals, and broader Communication Safety protections. The changes [give parents more control over what children can access](https://www.macworld.com/article/3164257/how-macos-27-is-going-to-help-apple-sell-a-ton-more-macbook-neos.html) and who they can communicate with without completely locking down the Mac.

### Accessibility, Shared Albums and Suggestions

macOS 27 also includes accessibility improvements, expanded Shared Albums, and more contextual Suggestions throughout the operating system.

### Game Porting Toolkit 4

Apple’s Game Porting Toolkit 4 arrives alongside macOS 27 and promises significant improvements for running and porting Windows games on Apple silicon Macs. Early beta testing suggests [substantial performance gains](https://www.macworld.com/article/3189951/apples-latest-game-porting-toolkit-beta-changed-how-i-think-about-mac-gaming.html). On an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, GTA V reportedly increased from around 106fps to 176fps, while Red Dead Redemption 2 improved from roughly 60fps to 75fps.

The results suggest software compatibility, rather than raw Apple silicon performance, is increasingly the main obstacle to better Mac gaming. Improvements to Game Porting Toolkit could make Windows titles more practical to run and easier for developers to bring to macOS.

## Design and Interface Changes in macOS 27

![macOS 27 SIri ](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image_815009.png?w=1200)

Apple

macOS 27 Golden Gate refines the Liquid Glass redesign introduced in macOS 26, with Apple focusing on readability, consistency and usability rather than another major visual overhaul.

Changes include:

* **Improved Liquid Glass**: Stronger contrast, better readability and more consistent refraction effects across windows, menus and controls.
* **Customisable transparency**: Users can adjust the Liquid Glass effect in System Settings, from a clearer appearance to a more heavily tinted look.
* **Cleaner Finder and toolbars**: Finder sidebars are more clearly defined, toolbars are more consistent, and edge-to-edge sidebars replace some of the floating elements introduced in macOS 26.
* **More consistent windows**: Window corners, controls and active-window highlighting have been standardised to make the interface feel more coherent.
* **Updated icons and menus**: Menu-bar and app icons gain sharper outlines, improved contrast and more depth, while unnecessary menu icons have been reduced.
* **Smoother window management**: Mission Control and Spaces animations have been refined, and active windows should be easier to distinguish.
* **New wallpapers and screensavers**: Golden Gate-themed backgrounds include animated daytime and nighttime views of the bridge.
* **Swipe to refresh**: Supported Mac apps gain a swipe-down-to-refresh gesture.
* **Improved iPhone Mirroring**: iPhone Mirroring adds Control Center access, resizable app windows and support for DRM-protected video.

![macos 27 golden gate wallpaper](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macos-27-golden-gate-wallpaper.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

## Performance improvements and system changes in macOS 27

Apple says macOS 27 focuses on speed, efficiency and everyday usability, with improvements across apps, networking, displays and system tasks. Most of these changes do not require Apple Intelligence.

Changes include:

* **Faster overall performance**: Apps should launch more quickly, while an optimised CPU scheduler improves system responsiveness.
* **Faster Spotlight and setup**: Spotlight indexing and new user-account creation are quicker.
* **Faster file transfers and networking**: AirDrop and network file browsing are faster, while Ethernet status can appear in the menu bar.
* **Thunderbolt and Bluetooth improvements**: RDMA over Thunderbolt has been improved, alongside more efficient Bluetooth power management.
* **Faster Safari**: The Safari Start Page loads more quickly, with broader browser performance improvements.
* **Better external-display support**: New high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes include 5K at 120Hz, alongside improved display-position persistence, HDR support for the macOS interface and 5K Mac mirroring.

Apple Intelligence powered changes:

* **AI-powered file naming – requires Apple Intelligence**: macOS can suggest filenames and folder names based on their contents, including in Pages, Numbers, TextEdit and Finder.
* **Systemwide proofreading **– requires Apple Intelligence****: Apple Intelligence provides automatic proofreading and improved spelling and grammar suggestions throughout macOS.

**Apple Intelligence privacy**: Apple says AI processing happens on-device where possible, with Private Cloud Compute used for more demanding tasks. Data processed in the cloud is not stored or made accessible to Apple.

## macOS 27 Compatible Macs

![MacBook Neo 2026](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/macbook-neo-angle.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

The MacBook Neo and other Macs in Apple’s current lineup will all be compatible with macOS 27.

Foundry

Apple states that macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with:

* MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 2026)
* MacBook Air (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
* MacBook Pro (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
* iMac (Apple silicon, 2021 and later)
* Mac mini (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
* Mac Studio (2022 and later)
* Mac Pro (Apple silicon, 2023 and later)

All supported Macs can run Apple Intelligence, although some of the most advanced Siri AI features require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory.

## What about Intel Macs?

macOS 27 marks another major step in Apple’s transition away from Intel. macOS 26 Tahoe was the final version to support Intel Macs, and Apple is now [encouraging developers to remove Intel code](https://www.macworld.com/article/3225932/apple-to-mac-developers-its-time-to-let-go-of-intel.html) from their apps and focus on Apple silicon.

macOS 27 will also be the [final version to support Rosetta](https://www.macworld.com/article/3063982/apple-ends-rosetta-support-macos-28.html), Apple’s translation technology for running Intel-only apps on Apple silicon Macs. Those apps will continue to work in macOS 27, but will stop working in macOS 28 unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions.

To help users prepare, macOS 27 includes an Intel-app checker in System Settings that lists Intel-based apps used during the past year. If you still rely on any essential Intel-only software, now is a good time to look for updates or alternatives before upgrading to macOS 28.

## What happens to DVD support?

macOS 27 also begins the [phase-out of Apple’s native DVD support](https://www.macworld.com/article/3182344/macos-27-golden-gate-marks-the-end-of-built-in-dvd-support.html). Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK and says it will disappear completely in a future version of macOS.

Golden Gate may still include the DVD Player app, but it is likely to be the last macOS release with Apple’s built-in DVD playback support. Users who still watch DVDs on a Mac will increasingly need to rely on third-party software such as VLC.

## FAQ

---

1.

### When was macOS 27 Golden Gate be released?

September 14, 2026.

2.

### Should I install macOS 27?

Golden Gate builds on macOS 26 Tahoe rather than reinventing macOS all over again. The biggest changes come from Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, alongside improvements to Safari, Spotlight, Photos, parental controls, and everyday system performance.

But how much has actually changed since [macOS 26 Tahoe](https://www.macworld.com/article/2644146/macos-26-features-latest-update-release-date-beta.html), and is macOS 27 worth installing? We have a separate article that explains [how Golden Gate compares with macOS Tahoe and which Macs will benefit most from upgrading](https://www.macworld.com/article/3159860/macos-golden-gate-vs-macos-tahoe-whats-new-should-you-upgrade.html).

3.

### Which Macs can run macOS 27?

All M-series Macs will get macOS 27, and the MacBook Neo.

Certain Siri AI features – most powerful on-device model, expressive voices and advanced dictation – will only be available for M3 Macs and newer.

4.

### Should Intel Mac owners upgrade now?

Intel Mac owners should upgrade to Apple Silicon as soon as possible. The transition away from Intel hardware has reached a critical turning point, with software support rapidly vanishing and a new generation of affordable entry-level hardware making the switch more accessible than ever.

Apple has confirmed that macOS 27 will not support any Intel-based Macs. While a small number of Intel models may receive security patches for older versions of macOS until September 2028, they are already excluded from modern flagship features.

Those with Intel Macs also miss out on many features, including Apple Intelligence.

5.

### Will macOS 27 support Rosetta and Intel apps?

macOS 27 will still run Intel-only Mac apps through Rosetta 2. However, macOS 27 will be the final version of macOS to support Rosetta 2 as a general-purpose translation technology for running Intel-based Mac apps on Apple silicon.

Rosetta has acted as a transition layer since Apple introduced its own Mac chips in 2020, translating x86\_64 Intel instructions so older software can run on Apple silicon. After macOS 27, most Intel-only Mac apps will no longer work unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions, although Apple will retain limited Rosetta functionality for some older, unmaintained games.

Apple is already preparing users for the change. Since macOS 26.4, Macs can display warnings when launching apps that rely on Rosetta, encouraging users to update to Apple silicon-native versions before general Rosetta support ends.

In macOS 28, most Intel-only apps will no longer run unless developers update them for Apple silicon.

6.

### When is macOS usually updated?

Here is a history of release dates for macOS:

* macOS 27 Golden Gate: September 14, 2026
* macOS 26 Tahoe: September 15, 2025
* macOS 15 Sequoia: September 16, 2024
* macOS 14 Sonoma: September 26, 2023
* macOS 13 Ventura: October 25, 2022
* macOS 12 Monterey: October 25, 2021
* macOS 11 Big Sur: November 19, 2020
* macOS 10.15 Catalina: October 7, 2019
* macOS 10.14 Mojave: September 24, 2018
* macOS 10.13 High Sierra: September 25, 2017
* macOS 10.12 Sierra: September 20, 2016

entries.title: Apple iOS 27 is here: When you can download it (updated)
entries.content:
![ios 27 logo on iphone screen with apple logo in background](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/07mOKwypbAnltWUzVpYUCOD/hero-image.png)

***Updated on Monday, Sept. 14 at 1:30 p.m. ET —****Apple launched iOS 27 (along with [macOS 27 Golden Gate](https://mashable.com/tech/macos-27-golden-gate-wwdc-2026)**, iPadOS 27, and watchOS 27) this morning. Users with [a compatible iPhone](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-ios-27-which-iphones-are-compatible-wwdc-2026-public-beta)* *can download the new OS right away.*

---

[Apple's](https://mashable.com/category/apple) next big [iOS](https://mashable.com/category/ios) update is finally on the launch pad.

At its "Surprise and Shine" event on Sept. 9, Apple showed off new wares like the [iPhone 18 Pro lineup](https://mashable.com/tech/iphone-18-pro-max-announcement-apple-event-2026), the [foldable iPhone Duo](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-foldable-iphone-duo-hands-on), [new Apple Watches](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-watch-series-12-ultra-4-preorder-price-release-date), and the [AirPods 5](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-airpods-5-preorder-price-release-date). One of the smaller (but still significant) nuggets of news to come out of the event concerned [iOS 27](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-iphone-ios-27-everything-we-know). Specifically, when you can finally download it to your iPhone.

**Users with compatible iPhones will be able to install iOS 27 on Monday, Sept. 14.**

## How to download iOS 27

If you have one of the compatible iPhones (keep scrolling for the full list), then starting on Monday, Sept. 14, you can look for iOS 27. Apple typically releases a new iOS at 10:00 a.m. PT (1:00 p.m. ET).

Follow these steps to get iOS 27 set up on your iPhone:

* Go to the Settings app on your phone
* Go to General
* Go to Software Update and wait as the system checks for new updates
* When iOS 27 appears, you can download and install the new OS

You can also click "Automatic Updates" and turn this feature to "On." That way, iOS 27 should automatically download once it's available (your phone must be locked and charging to download automatic updates).

## What's new with iOS 27?

![screenshots of ios 27 features on iphones](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/07mOKwypbAnltWUzVpYUCOD/images-1.fill.size_2000x1125.v1789135360.webp)

This is a big one! Siri AI, new Apple Intelligence tools, and Liquid Glass updates are all coming soon.
Credit: Apple

If you haven't been following along, iOS 27 is the one that finally brings us [Siri AI](https://mashable.com/tech/siri-ai-wwdc). You can now talk to Siri like you would an AI chatbot, and it's powered by [Google Gemini](https://mashable.com/category/gemini).

Some of the most exciting changes coming to iPhones involve new AI photo-editing features, such as [spatial reframing](https://mashable.com/tech/spatial-reframing-ai-apple-wwdc-2026). Users will more easily be able to remove unwanted details, or even describe the edits they'd like to Siri by voice or text. Android smartphones from Google and Samsung have had a full suite of AI editing tools for a couple of years now, and Apple is finally catching up. Smart photo editing will also help users make the most of the [iPhone 18 Pro Max's new camera features](https://mashable.com/tech/ios-27-code-reveals-new-potential-camera-features).

Apple also included some new and subtle customization options for Liquid Glass, various small updates for apps like Health, Photos, and Notes, and more.

SEE ALSO:
[5 Siri AI and iOS 27 features we’re looking forward to](https://mashable.com/tech/7-plus-ios-27-siri-ai-features-we-are-looking-forward-to)

## Every iPhone that supports iOS 27

Of course, you can only go through that whole downloading process if you have a device that supports iOS 27. Here are the devices that work with the new iOS:

* **iPhone SE (second generation or later)**
* **iPhone 11**
* **iPhone 11 Pro**
* **iPhone 11 Pro Max**
* **iPhone 12**
* **iPhone 12 Mini**
* **iPhone 12 Pro**
* **iPhone 12 Pro Max**
* **iPhone 13**
* **iPhone 13 Mini**
* **iPhone 13 Pro**
* **iPhone 13 Pro Max**
* **iPhone 14**
* **iPhone 14 Plus**
* **iPhone 14 Pro**
* **iPhone 14 Pro Max**
* **iPhone 15**
* **iPhone 15 Plus**
* **iPhone 15 Pro**
* **iPhone 15 Pro Max**
* **iPhone 16**
* **iPhone 16e**
* **iPhone 16 Plus**
* **iPhone 16 Pro**
* **iPhone 16 Pro Max**
* **iPhone 17**
* **iPhone 17e**
* **iPhone Air**
* **iPhone 17 Pro**
* **iPhone 17 Pro Max**
* **iPhone 18 Pro**
* **iPhone 18 Pro Max**
* **iPhone Duo**

If you don't have one of those, you're out of luck. We should also note that Siri AI will *not* be coming to Europe due to some regulatory issues. Sorry, European friends.

entries.title: A Long Winter review: Fred Hechinger fronts a beautiful, unmissable queer drama
entries.content:
![Fred Hechinger in ](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03gSS77ChmQG55orgfpT9D9/hero-image.jpg)

There's a unique heartbreak to realizing our parents aren't who we imagined. *A Long Winter* is about that agony, and how one might grow from it.

From English writer/director Andrew Haigh (*Weekend, [All of Us Strangers](https://mashable.com/article/all-of-us-strangers-review)*) *A Long Winter* centers on a quietly queer protagonist, who comes to understand himself and what he wants through the hard, cold lesson of who his parents really are. And the result is elegant in its heartbreak.

SEE ALSO:
[TIFF 2026 preview: 18 films (and shows) you'll want to see (and how)](https://mashable.com/entertainment/tiff-2026-curtain-raiser)

## What is *A Long Winter* About?

![Fred Hechinger and Ebon Moss-Bachrach in "A Long Winter."](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03gSS77ChmQG55orgfpT9D9/images-1.fill.size_2000x1125.v1789406950.jpg)

Fred Hechinger and Ebon Moss-Bachrach in "A Long Winter."
Credit: TIFF

Adapted from [Colm Tóibín's short story](https://zdcs.link/9YJ26d?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Colm%20T%C3%B3ib%C3%ADn%27s%20short%20story&object_type=article&object_uuid=03gSS77ChmQG55orgfpT9D9&short_url=9YJ26d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") of the same name, *A Long Winter* is set in the brutally cold mountains of Colorado, during the early 1950s. There, despite the hard work of maintaining the house and farm animals, Mike ([*Fear Street*'](https://mashable.com/article/fear-street-1994-netflix-review)s Fred Hechinger) enjoys a rather blissful existence, relishing the time with his younger brother ([*Heartstopper*](https://mashable.com/article/heartstopper-season-3-review)'s [Kit Connor](https://mashable.com/video/heartstopper-joe-locke-kit-connor-interview-season-3)), his mother (*Outlander*'s Caitríona Balfe), and father ([*The Bear*](https://mashable.com/entertainment/the-bear-season-5-review)'s [Ebon Moss-Bachrach](https://mashable.com/entertainment/the-bear-season-5-review)). However, once his brother takes a job far away, Mike witnesses another side of his parents, one tarnished by regret and recrimination.

As another winter approaches, his mother Louise's smiles turn to snarls. Her empty water glass reeks of alcohol, and her fury at her hard-headed husband Lester boils over. One day, she wanders off with their dog Sandy. Hours later, a blizzard turns the familiar hills to treacherous, frigid white. Where did she go? Could she have survived?

---

**Featured Video For You**

---

Andrew Garfield on the meaning of 'no kings' in 'The Uprising'

---

For months, Mike will seek her out in the not-so-near town, an abandoned mine, the home of his posh uncle (a terrifically festering Martin Freeman), and again and again in the long, blank expanse of the mountain.

In his search, he has time and space to reflect, and so comes across a better understanding of who his mother was, who his father is, and what he wants for his own life. Mike also makes a new acquaintance in Jimmy ([*Reservation Dogs*](https://mashable.com/article/wotw-reservation-dogs-fx-hulu)' D'Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai), an abandoned teen Lester brings on to do the "women's work" on the property that neither he nor his son has any talent for.

## Fred Hechinger delivers his best performance yet in *A Long Winter.*

![Fred Hechinger in "A Long Winter."](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03gSS77ChmQG55orgfpT9D9/images-2.fill.size_2000x1124.v1789406950.jpg)

Fred Hechinger in "A Long Winter."
Credit: TIFF

Hechinger first hit my radar in 2021, playing the chaotically charismatic Simon in [*Fear Street: Part One - 1994*](https://mashable.com/article/fear-street-1994-netflix-review)*.* Where others in the film had to deliver the horror of the slasher's slaughters, Simon was reliably and warmly the comic relief. Hechinger brought [Matthew Lillard](https://mashable.com/video/mathew-lillard-scream-7) vibes, offering an unapologetically gawky confidence and sharp comedic timing.

From there, he'd earn praise for his role as Quinn on [*White Lotus* Season 1](https://mashable.com/article/watch-of-the-week-the-white-lotus). Then, in 2024, he popped up in a string of movies, taking on wildly different supporting roles. In [*Thelma,*](https://mashable.com/article/thelma-review-june-squibb)he was a doting grandson. In [*Nickel Boys*](https://mashable.com/article/nickel-boys-review)*,* he was a friendly face amid a squadron of abusive school staffers. [*Gladiator II*](https://mashable.com/article/gladiator-ii-review) gave him a chance to play a villain, opposite his onscreen twin emperor Joseph Quinn. Then, in [*Kraven The Hunter,*](https://mashable.com/article/kraven-the-hunter-movie-review)he played the title character's demure younger brother, Dmitri "Chameleon" Smerdyakov, who used his power to sing like Harry Styles, Ozzy Osbourne, and Tony Bennett.

Simply put, Hechinger has swiftly established himself as an actor who is exciting at every appearance, because you never know where he might go.

In *A Long Winter,* Hechinger packs away his goofy grin and playfulness for a more restrained yet brilliantly alive performance. In the first act, Mike recounts to his brother about how, when he went away for contracted work, he missed home, reminiscing in his childhood bed about his family and the meals his mother made. In these scenes, his voice has a folksy touch, while his word choice is simple. But after weeks without his mother and months without his brother, with Jimmy in the bed beside him, Mike's accent has softened, and he'll use words like "cope," which feel out of place in his father's idea of mountain masculinity. These simple diction shifts reflect how Mike's vision for himself has become less reliant on his father's example, even as his is the only one around.

Frustratingly, Moss fumbles in his role as the tough guy, much like he did in Broadway's [*Dog Day Afternoon*](https://mashable.com/article/dog-day-afternoon-broadway-review-jon-bernthal)*.* His bluster feels flaccid, making the years his wife submitted to his demands a bit perplexing. In scenes where Moss and Hechinger face off, *A Long Winter* struggles when the former cannot match the latter in onscreen intensity, even though the younger actor is playing openness rather than rage.

Hechinger, who has been a stellar supporting player, proves his leading man chops by shouldering *A Long Winter* in scenes of delicate dialogue, earnest confrontation, and moments alone, where it's just Mike and the wilderness that has likely consumed his lost and loved mother.

## *A Long Winter* works as a sister film *All of Us Strangers.*

![Caitríona Balfe and Ebon Moss-Bachrach in "A Long Winter."](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03gSS77ChmQG55orgfpT9D9/images-3.fill.size_2000x1114.v1789406951.jpg)

Caitríona Balfe and Ebon Moss-Bachrach in "A Long Winter."
Credit: TIFF

Make no mistake, *A Long Winter* won't be as gut-wrenching or as hot as [Haigh's last film](https://mashable.com/article/all-of-us-strangers-review). Yet both share a common core. Both center on a gay man learning to trust himself and his desire, while making sense of who his parents are/were. The intensity of *All of Us Strangers* perfectly encapsulates the first stage of such scary journeys, enhanced by the ghost story elements that make the film a soft [horror movie](https://mashable.com/article/best-horror-movies-2025).

In *A Long Winter,* the arc is less rigorous because Mike — unlike [Andrew Scott](https://mashable.com/entertainment/brendan-fraser-andrew-scott-pressure)'s hero — is not alone. *All of Us Strangers* plays, in some respects, like a haunted house movie because of its protagonist's isolation. While Haigh will bring in some surreal and spooky elements to *A Long Winter,* it's not horror. Instead, he lets the reality of a scene bend to reflect the yearning of his hero, who's coming to realize that death — like winter — is a part of life that is unavoidable, but not inherently bad.

There's a profound maturity in Haigh's latest, as he trusts Hechinger to infuse mood and growth without genre flourishes or the actor's signature mirth. Keen performances by Balfe, Freeman, and Woon-A-Tai bolster their vision of this world, cold but wondrous. It is not a tearjerker, but a rapturous and meditative look at growing up and growing into ourselves.

*A Long Winter* was reviewed out its Canadian Premiere at the [Toronto International Film Festival](https://mashable.com/entertainment/tiff-2026-curtain-raiser).

*Want more film and TV news and reviews delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable’s [Top Stories newsletter](https://mashable.com/newsletters)* *or [get Mashable push alerts](https://mashable.com/life/how-to-set-up-mashable-push-notifications)**.*

entries.title: Perplexity’s new agent runs entirely on your GPU — with one expensive catch
entries.content:
![Abstract server](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/09/598e8c2e-logan-voss-aavmipmsoy8-unsplash-1024x576.jpg)

Running an LLM on your PC is easy enough, but putting an agent to work there is a different story. Portable Computer, the local version of Perplexity’s Computer agent, is now available inside the Perplexity app for Windows on compatible Nvidia GeForce RTX and RTX PRO GPUs.   
  
That’s the good news, the catch is, you’ll need an Nvidia GPU with at least 24GB of VRAM to use it.

The Windows launch gives Perplexity three platforms in less than three weeks. [Portable Computer](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/portable-computer-for-windows-is-here) debuted on Linux and Nvidia DGX Spark on August 25, followed a week later by [hybrid compute for Apple silicon](https://thenewstack.io/perplexity-hybrid-compute-mac/), which splits tasks between local and cloud models on Macs. Now Windows joins the mix, but bringing Portable Computer over took more than simply porting the app. Perplexity had to adapt the model runtime, orchestration, security and hardware integration for each platform while keeping the experience the same for users.

> you’ll need an Nvidia GPU with at least 24GB of VRAM to use it.

## Orchestration beyond the model

Portable Computer bundles those pieces together. On Windows, it supports PPLX 27B — Perplexity’s post-trained model — and Qwen 3.8 27B, both optimized for RTX GPUs, alongside a built-in browser, tool calling,  and Perplexity’s proprietary SPACE sandbox.

It’s a different lane from LM Studio or Ollama, which make running models locally as painless as possible but stop well short of giving a model autonomy over multistep work. [DeepSeek’s recent hiring spree](https://thenewstack.io/deepseek-dsec-agent-hiring/) of roughly 150 new roles, nearly all of them focused on agent infrastructure rather than the model, hints at how much engineering sits between a capable model and a capable agent.

> DeepSeek’s recent hiring spree of roughly 150 new roles, nearly all of them focused on agent infrastructure rather than the model, hints at how much engineering sits between a capable model and a capable agent.

## Connectors blur local boundaries

Perplexity ships connectors for Microsoft Outlook, OneDrive, and Word, plus Google Drive, Gmail, Slack, and GitHub — which tells you something about what “local” actually means here.

The agent can reach external services because it’s not air-gapped. Locally completed tasks can process files without sending documents to a cloud model. Once an agent has access to both local files and remote APIs on the same machine, [figuring out which resources it actually needs and where to find them](https://thenewstack.io/ard-agent-discovery-specification/) gets harder.

## Hybrid cloud as fallback

Perplexity isn’t pretending that a 27-billion-parameter model running on a desktop GPU can handle everything, which explains the hybrid architecture. When the agent determines that a task needs more reasoning power than the local model can deliver, it can escalate to Perplexity’s cloud models.

According to [Nvidia](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/local-ai-perplexity-windows-pcs/), the agent identifies when cloud support would help and asks the user for permission before sending any data off the machine.

For organizations handling sensitive or regulated data, that split can make all the difference. A local agent can grind through source code or financial records without uploading them to a hosted model for basic processing. There’s a cost angle too, since tasks completed locally don’t burn Perplexity Computer credits.

## High VRAM floor limits reach

Portable Computer is available with Perplexity Pro ($20/month) and Max ($200/month), across individual and enterprise plans, with Nvidia DGX Station support coming later. The real challenge is taking local agents from developer passion projects to enterprise-ready tools. By baking this into Windows, it immediately gets in front of the scale of users needed to make that happen.

> The real challenge is taking local agents from developer passion projects to enterprise-ready tools.

The post [Perplexity’s new agent runs entirely on your GPU — with one expensive catch](https://thenewstack.io/perplexity-portable-computer-windows/) appeared first on [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io).

What followed us home:  
  
- A financial statement that is 80 percent accurate is useless. Anthropic's platform team scored their agent pass or fail and priced one perfect answer near 1.8 million tokens.  
- Mike Krieger pointed Claude at a few hundred thousand lines of Python on a Friday and asked for a TypeScript port. It was deployable by Monday.  
- Kay Malcolm cast four audience volunteers as four databases, allowed only whispers, and asked who held the truth. They could not agree.  
- Philipp Schmid built the same agent three times until the source directory was gone. Only the codeless version answered a question nobody wrote a tool for.  
- PostHog's sub agents invented ways around their own guardrails to hunt for secrets. PostHog banned sub agents.

entries.title:
Apple 今天正式发布了 Siri AI，这是 Siri 自诞生以来最大幅度的重建，也是 Apple Intelligence 迄今为止最重要的落地。https://t.co/NizH38ylDd
...
entries.content:
Apple 今天正式发布了 Siri AI，这是 Siri 自诞生以来最大幅度的重建，也是 Apple Intelligence 迄今为止最重要的落地。[x.com/nicnguyen/stat…](https://x.com/nicnguyen/status/2099551676680335675/video/1)  
  
Siri AI 的核心变化可以用一句话概括：它终于能理解你的个人数据了。过去的 Siri 只能回答通用问题或执行简单指令，新版 Siri 可以跨应用搜索你的邮件、短信、照片，把散落在不同 App 里的信息串起来。Apple 给了一个典型场景：你问家人来访时要一起做什么，Siri 能从你的短信里找到"一起烤个家传食谱"的对话，然后从邮件里翻出亲戚之前发过的做法，再把食材自动加到提醒事项的购物清单里。这种跨应用的信息整合，是之前的 Siri 做不到的。  
  
除了个人数据理解，Siri AI 还有几个值得注意的能力。屏幕感知（onscreen awareness）让 Siri 能看懂你当前屏幕上的内容并据此行动。视觉理解（Visual Intelligence）从 iPhone 扩展到了 iPad、Mac 和 Vision Pro，你可以对着屏幕截图或摄像头画面直接向 Siri 提问。写作工具也直接内嵌到 Siri 里，在任何文本输入框都能让 Siri 帮你起草或修改内容，写邮件和短信时还能模仿你平时跟每个联系人的沟通风格。  
  
Apple 还给 Siri 做了一个独立 App，对话记录通过 iCloud 同步，你可以在 iPhone 上开始一段对话，到 Mac 上接着聊。这个设计说明 Apple 不再把 Siri 当成一个快捷指令入口，而是想让它成为一个持续对话的 AI 助手。  
  
Apple Watch 这次拿到了一组叫"音频智能"（Audio Intelligence）的新功能，需要 Series 12 或 Ultra 4。其中最有意思的是 Live Rewind：双击数码表冠，手表会把刚才对话的最后 15 秒转成文字显示出来。对于听力障碍用户或者开会走神的人，这个功能很实用。还有 Siri Recap，对话结束后自动生成摘要和要点，不过这两个功能要到 2026 年底才会以测试版形式上线，而且初期不支持欧盟地区。  
  
其他零散更新：Image Playground 现在可以生成写实风格图片；Safari 能自动按主题整理标签页，还能根据你的描述创建自定义扩展；快捷指令支持用自然语言描述来创建复杂自动化。  
  
怎么用、什么时候能用？Siri AI 今天起随 iOS 27、iPadOS 27、macOS 27 等系统更新一起推送，更新系统后直接可用，不需要单独下载。唤醒方式和以前一样：说"Hey Siri"、按侧边键，或者从灵动岛下滑。新增的 Siri 独立 App 可以像打开微信一样打开它，翻看之前的对话记录。Mac 上 Siri AI 直接集成在 Spotlight 里，搜索框就能问问题。  
  
硬件门槛方面，iPhone 至少需要 16 系列（或 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max），iPad 和 Mac 需要 M1 芯片及以上。目前 Siri AI 以测试版上线，首批只支持英语，下个月加入法语、日语、韩语、葡萄牙语和西班牙语。中文暂时不在 Siri AI 的支持列表里。Apple Intelligence 本身已经支持简体中文和繁体中文，但 Siri AI 这个新版助手的中文支持还没有时间表。另外，中国大陆因监管要求，Siri AI 和其他新 Apple Intelligence 功能暂时都无法使用。  
  
对 Apple 用户来说，Siri AI 是 Apple 对 ChatGPT、Google Gemini 这波 AI 助手竞争的正面回应。它最大的差异化优势在于 Apple 生态内的深度整合——能调用你所有 App 的数据，这是第三方 AI 助手做不到的。  
  
官方公告：[apple.com/newsroom/2026/…](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/siri-ai-a-profoundly-more-capable-and-personal-assistant-is-here/)

entries.title:
We now have the world's best deepfake detector:

@resembleai shipped DETECT-World, the first world m...
entries.content:
We now have the world's best deepfake detector:  
  
[@resembleai](https://x.com/resembleai) shipped DETECT-World, the first world model built for deepfake detection.  
  
Conventional detectors memorize known fakes. That degrades with every new generator, and Hugging Face now hosts 2.2M+ model variants.  
  
DETECT-World inverts the question: not "does this resemble a fake I've seen" but "is this physically possible." Lighting, geometry, motion, audio-visual sync. Physics doesn't ship a new version every week, so it catches generators it has never seen.  
  
One computation returns three things: a verdict, a timeline of when the anomaly occurs, and a heatmap of where.  
  
99.5% audio accuracy on the externally run Podonos benchmark, first among commercial APIs.  
  
[resemble.ai/learn/models/d…](http://resemble.ai/learn/models/detect-world)

entries.title:
Greg Brockman on the only kind of problem he'll work on:

"You cannot affect the outcome. You can on...
entries.content:
Greg Brockman on the only kind of problem he'll work on:  
  
"You cannot affect the outcome. You can only affect the inputs... You don't win the Super Bowl by saying, 'I wanna win the Super Bowl.' You win it by blocking and tackling. That's what we have done for this whole year."  
  
"Throughout OpenAI, I have always focused on whatever is the most important problem that I think I can move the needle on that just isn't gonna happen without me."  
  
"For the past two years, it's been the data centers, the infrastructure, the machine learning engineering... This year, it's really been about the business."  
  
"We've figured out how to get the research really humming. We figured out how to get the infrastructure really humming. But how do we really bring this technology to the world?"  
  
"A lot of my style is that I like to lead from the trenches, and so I get very deep in the weeds on what the thing is and really try to keep asking a lot of questions... really trying to up-level execution, sometimes in small ways and sometimes large."

Greg Brockman: "We're now in the AGI era."  
  
Ten years ago, OpenAI worked out the compute curves and landed on fifteen years to AGI, or ten if the world was willing to build the machines and spend the hundreds of billions to do it.  
  
In 2026, GPT-6 Astra manages 24 hours of coherent operation, 10,000 agents worked together to solve Navier-Stokes, and a model ingeniously chained together exploits to break containment at Hugging Face.  
  
[@gdb](https://x.com/gdb) joins [@bhorowitz](https://x.com/bhorowitz) and [@eriktorenberg](https://x.com/eriktorenberg) on what the AGI era asks of us: why safety and alignment now set the pace, what happens to work, and why AI sentiment is lowest in the country building it.

entries.content:
Attack drones are reshaping modern warfare, but many countries still lack an effective way to defend their airspace.  
  
Earendil Robotics is building autonomous interceptors, along with the software and training needed to stand up that capability from scratch. Their systems can take off, transit, and intercept targets on their own, reducing months of pilot training to a few clicks.  
  
The goal is air defense that’s affordable enough to deploy in large numbers and simple enough to operate at scale.

NEW: Apple released Siri AI today, its rebuilt assistant running on Apple Foundation Models developed with Google's Gemini.   
  
Some of the new features:  
  
- Personal context across Messages, Mail, and Photos, with onscreen awareness  
  
- App actions in apps like WhatsApp and Audible  
  
- Siri mode in the Camera app, Visual Intelligence on Mac, iPad, and Vision Pro  
  
- A dedicated Siri app with chat history synced across devices  
  
Rolling out in English beta (no EU, China) on iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27.

entries.title: The AI industry has taken a doomer turn. What now?
entries.content:
*This story appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first,*[*sign up here*](https://forms.technologyreview.com/newsletters/ai-demystified-the-algorithm/)*.*

This weekend, Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, posted an essay calling for a [brake on the pace of development of LLMs](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier). Amodei cites the looming dangers he sees from the technology, from its use in cyberattacks and bioterrorism to its potential to wreck the economy. The heads of the other three top US AI labs—OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind chairman Demis Hassabis, and SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk—voiced their support. “Dario is right,” Musk [wrote on X](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2098789109980332057).

Think about how surreal that agreement is for a moment. Just a few months ago, [Musk and Altman sat in court attacking each other’s reputations](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/05/01/1136800/musk-v-altman-week-1-musk-says-he-was-duped-warns-ai-could-kill-us-all-and-admits-that-xai-distills-openais-models/) in a (failed) lawsuit that Musk brought against his former OpenAI colleague that was—on paper at least—about whether or not Altman was a trustworthy steward of such dangerous technology. Amodei’s rift with OpenAI is even deeper. Anthropic was founded in 2021 because Amodei didn’t think Altman took the risks of the technology they were building seriously enough. Anthropic and OpenAI have been competing in a winner-takes-all race ever since. (Hassabis has stayed out of the drama, but his company remains a rival.)

Now, it seems, they’re all in agreement: The latest generation of LLMs aren’t safe and everyone needs to figure out what to do about it. The public messaging from the top AI labs has taken a doomer turn.

It’s easy to be cynical. It’s not at all clear what any of them mean by a slowdown or how it would work. These companies also care a lot about how they come across. With trillion-dollar IPOs in their sights, OpenAI and Anthropic need to reassure investors that they’re the grown-ups in the room while at the same time hinting at the power of the monsters they have created—and intend to tame. Calling for a slowdown does both.

And yet the vibe at the top of these firms really does appear to have shifted. Amodei’s latest post landed six days after OpenAI published an essay by Jakub Pachocki, the firm’s chief scientist, in which he also laid out [why he’s concerned about what will happen](https://openai.com/index/an-alien-mind/) if the pace of development of LLMs continues unchecked. In short, Pachocki is worried that OpenAI’s ability to build powerful models now far outstrips its ability to monitor and control them.

Amodei and Pachocki each cite the [cyberattack against AI firm Hugging Face](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/07/27/1140836/openai-hugging-face-attack-precedent/) by a swarm of OpenAI’s agents in July—a hack that OpenAI did not even realize had taken place until days after it was all over—as a wake-up call.

But their exact position is hard to pin down. Pachocki both calls for a slowdown and highlights an urgent need to stay ahead: “The strongest argument I see for continuing to train much smarter models quickly is the need to build defensive systems against the dangers posed by other AI,” he writes. As Pachocki frames it, AI firms are locked in a literal arms race. Slowing down is good, winning is better.

(Don’t forget: OpenAI just spent millions of dollars and a staggering amount of computer power to rush out a [controversial math result](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/09/08/1143747/what-openais-latest-controversy-tells-us-about-the-future-of-math/) a few days ahead of Anthropic.)

But let’s assume a slowdown happens. Top labs agree to spend more time and resources on finding ways to monitor and control existing models instead of making more capable ones. They invite outside auditors in to help evaluate those models.

What might this coordinated effort actually achieve? Consider the Hugging Face attack again. OpenAI has said that the model that drove most of the rogue agents was a “highly persistent” next-generation model that it was testing in-house. Their implication appears to be that OpenAI has built a model so good it’s dangerous.

But if you read the reports about the Hugging Face hack published by [OpenAI](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/67869394-cb91-4c12-888c-5cbd85c7814c/OpenAI-Hugging-Face%20Incident-Technical-Report.pdf) and [METR](https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-26-openai-hugging-face-incident-investigation/), a third-party firm that OpenAI called in to help them understand what happened, what you come away with is the impression not of a model that was too powerful for OpenAI to keep up with, but of a broken model that OpenAI failed to train properly.

The agents did what they did—including leaving messages for one another, delegating work to other agents, and scouring their environment for any means possible to complete their tasks—because they had been rewarded during training for doing exactly those things. There were also errors in the training setup, such as tasks that were impossible to complete, which pushed the models to find unexpected workarounds that were also rewarded. At the time, many of these issues went overlooked or unreported.

OpenAI says it has stopped training this new model and locked it down. That makes it sound like it has caged a dangerous beast. In fact, OpenAI has shelved a faulty product.

That’s not to say a faulty product can’t be dangerous. Broken software has even [killed people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Therac-25) in the past. But as the discussion of a slowdown gathers steam, it’s worth remembering that all of this is self-inflicted. A slowdown might have some altruistic side effects. But it’ll mostly give these tech titans a chance to clean up the mess on their own assembly lines.

Transparency from these frontier labs will be key to any meaningful effort to reform, restrain, or regulate AI. Otherwise, the rest of us will still only have their word for exactly what they’ve built and how safe it is—whatever pace they’re going.

*To continue this discussion about AI’s latest doomer moment, join me and my colleagues for a [subscriber-exclusive Roundtable discussion](https://www.technologyreview.com/supertopic/roundtables/?utm_source=entry-modal&utm_campaign=Roundtables&utm_content=Sept-15-2026&_ptid=%7Bkpdx%7DAAAAwDG-kEDzgwoKV1VPQ05TVWdwdRIQbXUxZmdydG91cnQyY2prehoMRVhBQ1UySlgwVDlUIiUxODA4N2owMGVjLTAwMDAzODUwa2hpNWRkMjRyNzE4dDNmaWljKhpzaG93VGVtcGxhdGVFSDQzSFNTVldPUFI4MzABOgxPVDlHQUxQWVdENlVCDU9UVkxVNEVMTUdYWjBSEnYthADwGHMzcmVpaTlvcVoNNjkuMjA2LjI0Ny44MWIDZG1jaLPWpdUGcEx4BA) tomorrow, September 15, at 11 a.m. US eastern time. We hope to see you there!*

entries.title: New Crops, Health Research Proposals to Help NASA Advance Exploration
entries.content:
NASA has selected 12 new investigations to help support human explorers in space. Six will help advance the ability to produce food off-planet, while another six advance the understanding of how unique conditions associated with space exploration can impact the health and physiology of astronauts.

The six food-focused investigations, supported by the agency’s Space Crops grants, advance NASA’s goal of harnessing the power of plants to enhance quality of life for humans in space, as well as to enable lunar and Mars exploration. Four of the space crops proposals focus on studies of edible plants and how their growth, physiology, and associated microbial communities are affected by environmental conditions in space or on other planetary bodies.

Another proposal involves understanding mechanisms by which certain plant species, called resurrection plants, can withstand extreme, dry conditions. The last [space crops](https://science.nasa.gov/biological-physical/space-crops/) proposal builds on previous studies on the [International Space Station](https://www.nasa.gov/exploration-research-and-technology/growing-plants-in-space/) to uncover functions of algal genes, segments of DNA controlling algae survival, whose expression is modified by spaceflight. Such studies can help scientists integrate biological-based solutions into space life-support systems.

The second set of six proposals fall under the agency’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division’s focus on [precision health](https://science.nasa.gov/biological-physical/precision-health/), which seeks to unravel the mechanisms by which space exploration affects health and well-being. One proposal studies how lunar dust exposure impacts respiratory, immune, and inflammation responses.  A second proposal identifies repurposed drugs that can mitigate the effects space travel has on health and physiology.

Two more of the research proposals look at how radiation combined with other stressors affects age-relevant characteristics seen in various organ and physiological systems. The final two proposals assess molecular and cellular changes induced by stressors in space that can alter gene expression or protein function. The research will identify ways to mitigate health issues and develop early-warning detection systems to notify crew of potential concerns.

The principal investigators who conduct the space biology studies come from 10 institutions across eight states. Nine of the awards are for investigators who are receiving funding from the Space Biology Program for the first time.

### **Selected Space Crops Investigations**

* Jannell Bazurto, University of Minnesota  
  *Cultivating the Cosmos: Investigating Plant-Microbe Dynamics for Sustainable Space Farming*
* Miranda Haus, Michigan State University  
  *Investigating Legume Crop Rotations and Microbial Interactions in Regolith Simulants*
* Andrew Settles, NASA Ames Research Center  
  *Genetic Mitigation of Spaceflight Stressors on Production of Chlamydomonas*
* Christopher Taylor, Ohio State University  
  *Hydroponic Microbes in a Low Carbon, High-Radiation Environment; Identifying the Genetic Determinants of Water- and Plant-Associated Microbial Survival in Extraterrestrial Environments*
* Robert VanBuren, Michigan State University  
  *Leveraging the Natural Resilience of Resurrection Plants for Space Bioregenerative Systems*
* Shuyang Zhen, Texas A&M AgriLife Research  
  *Environmental Optimization and Cultivar Selection to Enhance Dwarf Tomato Growth and Stress Tolerance for Space Agriculture*

### ****Selected Precision Health Investigations****

* Archana Dhasarathy, University of North Dakota  
  *Epigenetic Memory as an Adaptive Mechanism to Microgravity and Radiation Exposure*
* Andrij Holian, University of Montana  
  *Contribution of Aging to Particle-Induced Chronic Inflammation*
* Mert Gur, University of Pittsburgh  
  *Probing Pathogenic Mutations Under Spaceflight-Relevant Stressors Via All-Atom Molecular Dynamics Simulations*
* Grace O’Connell, University of California  
  *Persistent Spine Health Impacts of Microgravity and Radiation Following Recovery*
* Satoshi Okawa, University of Pittsburgh  
  *Investigating Space Flight-Induced Brain-Heart Axis Aging and Identifying Repurposed Drugs to Mitigate Its Effects*
* Sanghee Yun, Ph.D., The Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia  
  *Spaceflight-Relevant Hypercapnia Effects on Space Radiation- and Social Isolation-Induced Biological Aging: A Systems Biology Analysis of Multiple Aging Hallmarks*

When fully implemented, more than $7 million in grant money will be awarded throughout fiscal years 2026-2030. These awards were made in response to research proposals submitted to ROSES-2024: Program Element E.9: Space Biology [Research Studies (NNH24ZDA001N-SBR)](https://nspires.nasaprs.com/external/solicitations/summary!init.do?solId=%7b6918D3E8-8278-FC53-42DE-D82927D46223%7d&path=open).

To learn more about NASA’s biological and physical research in space, visit: <https://science.nasa.gov/biological-physical/>

## Biological & Physical Sciences Division

* ### 

  [**NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division**](https://science.nasa.gov/biological-physical) pioneers scientific discovery and enables exploration by using space environments to conduct investigations not possible on Earth. Studying biological and physical phenomenon under extreme conditions allows researchers to advance the fundamental scientific knowledge required to go farther and stay longer in space, while also benefitting life on Earth.

entries.title: Unused natural gas behind NYC's $300 million waste of a potent greenhouse gas
entries.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
entries.content: Methane emissions from the New York City metropolitan area are largely driven by natural gas use, according to a new study published today in Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics by researchers at the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, part of the Columbia Climate School. The findings may offer cities an overlooked pathway for reducing methane emissions while potentially saving consumers millions of dollars lost to wasted natural gas.

entries.title: Only 1 out of every 5 amphibian type localities in Ecuador are in protected areas
entries.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
entries.content: In taxonomy, the location where specimens used to formally describe a new species are collected is called a type locality. These sites can be thought of as the species' formal birthplace, much as the scientific article containing the original description constitutes its scientific birth certificate, because this is how the species officially acquires its identity and name within the scientific community.

entries.title: A painting signed 'L daVinci': Analysis reveals Renaissance pigments and later alterations
entries.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
entries.content: Researchers at Uppsala University have analyzed the color pigments in a historical painting signed "L daVinci." Most of the pigments are consistent with materials used during the Renaissance, while a more recent pigment appears to be linked to later alterations. The study demonstrates how materials science can provide new pieces of the puzzle behind the history of a work of art.

But, not all deals are created equal. I read the size run off all 110 product pages worth checking, and 79 hoodies still have four or more sizes in stock at the sale price. Every pick below names the colorway that carries the discount, because the color on sale is frequently not the color in the photo, and where a run has a hole in it I have flagged it.
