entries.title: Arborists use supersonic air to save 300-year-old tree that survived American Revolution
entries.content:
A centuries’ old “[witness tree](https://www.popsci.com/environment/can-trees-predict-eclipse/)” that survived not only the [Revolutionary War](https://www.popsci.com/science/new-2026-quarters/) but a [direct hit from lightning](https://www.popsci.com/environment/how-many-trees-killed-by-lightning/) is facing yet another existential threat. Ironically, the famous oak in Eutaw Springs, South Carolina, is struggling to survive due to the strategies conservationists first used when attempting to preserve it decades ago.

The nearly 300-year-old tree was already nearing its semicentennial on September 8, 1781, when around 2,000 British and 2,500 American troops met at the [Battle of Eutaw Springs](https://www.battlefields.org/learn/revolutionary-war/battles/eutaw-springs). Believed to be the American Revolution’s last open-field engagement, the vicious combat was later remembered by colonial Maj. Gen. Nathanael Greene as “by far, the hottest action I ever saw, and the most bloody for the numbers engaged.” Records indicate 1,461 troops were killed, wounded, captured, or missing by the end of the conflict—although both sides claimed victory.

“That tree probably took a few lead balls itself,” arborist Aron Landsaw recently said in an [Associated Press](https://www.yoursun.com/arcadia/news/preservationists-are-working-to-extend-the-life-of-a-rare-revolutionary-war-witness-tree/article_129b4266-db31-59be-99b1-21704a3bb516.html) profile.

![Old chains being subsumed into tree trunk](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Witness-Tree-Chain.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

*The original support chains had begun to suffocate the tree itself. Credit: [SavATree](https://www.savatree.com/about-us/news/savatree-arborists-rescue-300-year-old-revolutionary-war-witness-tree/)* KRIS MEADE

Landsaw and other conservationists are working to preserve the 45-foot-tall tree from succumbing to lingering injuries. About 50 years ago, lightning struck its base and almost split the oak in half. In an attempt to save the tree, workers at the time wrapped its splintered branches in a series of steel chains and cables. Although the strategy successfully granted the oak a reprieve, it grew so much over the last five decades that those metal lashes are cutting into the tree itself. In some areas, the cabling is now completely encased in bark.

“The chains and cables are actually choking it out. It can’t nutrients up from the soil,” explained Landsaw.

As part of the [nation’s 250th anniversary](https://www.popsci.com/technology/worlds-largest-steam-locomotive-tour-2026/), South Carolina partnered with the American Battlefield Trust and New York state-based arborists to once again bring the oak tree back from the brink of death. This time, the strategy is more high-tech than metal chains. Using specialized equipment to generate supersonic air, workers have essentially loosened all the heavily compacted earth around the tree’s roots. From there, they added a nutrient-rich kelp concoction into the dirt to further bolster the oak’s health.

![Live oak 'witness tree' on sunny day in field in South Carolina](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Witness-Tree-Full.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

*The new accessories will divert any future lightning strikes away from the tree. Credit: [SavATree](https://www.savatree.com/about-us/news/savatree-arborists-rescue-300-year-old-revolutionary-war-witness-tree/)* KRIS MEADE

Other additions were tapped directly into the tree’s primary branches. These small, strategically placed lightning rods embedded into the oak are strung together with copper cables that all connect to a primary grounded copper rod located about 10 feet away from the tree. The odd-looking accessories are intended to prevent a repeat of the incident from 50 years ago.

“If lightning does hit it, it’ll run down the copper cables and dissipate into the ground,” said Landsaw.

The last phase will involve connecting a new set of reinforcement cables into the branches before carefully getting rid of the old chainwork. The replacement cables will all connect in the center so that the tree will remain flexible during wind gusts. No tree lives forever, but with the extra TLC and a little luck, the historic oak could easily bear witness to another 100 years of history.

The post [Arborists use supersonic air to save 300-year-old tree that survived American Revolution](https://www.popsci.com/environment/supersonic-air-saves-tree-revolutionary-war/) appeared first on [Popular Science](https://www.popsci.com).

entries.title: iOS 27: Major features, compatible iPhones, updates, and more
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

Apple unveiled iOS 27 at [WWDC on June 8, 2026](https://www.macworld.com/article/3154372/apple-event-wwdc-2026-live-blog.html). It immediately entered a beta-testing phase, and was widely released on September 14.

There are three main sets of features in this update: Siri AI, which is an entirely new Siri architecture with a dedicated Siri app, new features for parental safety, and a big emphasis on system improvements like faster performance and a lot of quality-of-life features users have been asking for.

iOS 27 will support every iPhone back to the iPhone 11 and iPhone SE (2nd generation), although some Apple Intelligence and Siri features will require newer hardware.

This hub covers everything Apple has confirmed for iOS 27, including new features, compatible iPhones, beta updates, Apple Intelligence improvements and what’s changing with Siri. We also cover notable discoveries from the beta and the latest rumors ahead of launch.

## What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance

* **Siri AI**: Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history.
* **Apple Intelligence across apps**: Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance.
* **Smarter Photos editing**: Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally.
* **Child safety and parental controls**: New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools designed to give parents more control.
* **System Improvements**: Apple has made many system operations faster and more efficient, which will be especially noticeable on older phones. Battery life may be longer, and there are dozens of small quality-of-life improvements throughout the system and its apps.

## iOS 27 release date: When did Apple release iOS 27?

* September 14, 2026

Apple made iOS 27 widely available on September 14 at around 10am Pacific Time.

## iOS 27 beta – What’s new in the latest beta?

* Latest beta: None, but iOS 27.1 beta should be available soon

Apple has several “Audio Intelligence” features coming to the new Apple Watch series 12 and Ultra 4 in an update later this year. Also, a new Health app, fully redesigned with AI insights at its core, is expected this year as well. Those things, as well as the software features required for the iPhone Duo, are likely to be in iOS 27.1

## Siri AI in iOS 27

![Siri AI inside the Dynamic Island in iOS 27](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Siri-AI-iOS-27.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

By far the biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI – an entirely new architecture for Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational, and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web.

### Siri AI features

* **More natural conversations**: Siri AI can understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands.
* **Personal context**: Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message.
* **Onscreen awareness**: Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article.
* **Camera intelligence**: A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees.
* **More capable app actions**: Siri can perform tasks within apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It can, for example, edit a recently sent message, add a song to a playlist or handle more complex Apple Music requests.
* **Better general knowledge and web answers**: Siri can use information from the web to answer questions about recent events and tackle more specific or complicated queries than before.
* **Conversation history across devices**: A dedicated Siri app lets users revisit previous conversations, pin important chats and continue conversations across Apple devices using iCloud syncing.
* **More natural Siri voices**: Siri gains more expressive voices, with controls on compatible devices for adjusting speaking pace and expressiveness. Voice customisation requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.
* **Improved dictation**: Better speech recognition, automatic punctuation, capitalisation and formatting allow users to dictate more naturally when converting speech into text.
* **AI-assisted message replies**: Siri can compose contextual replies in Messages using the conversation, personal information and web searches. Shortcuts can also automate replies to selected contacts, although manual Siri-assisted replies allow users to check and edit the response before it is sent.

Read about [what happened when we made Siri AI Answer all our Messages](https://www.macworld.com/article/3205200/i-made-siri-ai-automatically-answer-all-my-messages-heres-what-happened.html).

### How good is Siri AI?

Siri AI represents a significant improvement over the old Siri, particularly when handling conversational questions, current information, and personal context. It also has a dedicated app where you can see and continue previous conversations, upload images or documents, and more.

Even in our [early tests during the beta](https://www.macworld.com/article/3164693/siri-ai-is-both-impressive-and-disappointing.html), Siri AI proved to be much more helpful and useful.

It’s definitely one of the biggest reasons to upgrade to iOS 27, potentially changing Siri from a basic voice-command system into a more general way of interacting with the iPhone.

Apple’s approach to AI safety also appears more restrained than some rival chatbots, with Siri designed to avoid excessive flattery, pretending to be human, or responding inappropriately to potentially harmful requests.

However, Siri AI is launching as a “beta” feature and still requires a bit of polish. It’s also only available in U.S. English at first, with a handful of other languages/regions coming in October with iOS 27.1.

**Regional Siri AI availability**

Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the EU. It will also remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory issues. The first release only supports the U.S. English language, but several other languages are coming with the iOS 27.1 update in October.

### Siri AI compatibility

Siri AI requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later, and the “new expressive voices” feature requires an iPhone 17 Pro or the new iPhone 18 Pro.

## Apple Intelligence across apps

As well as Siri AI, the enhanced Apple Intelligence will also power new features in Apple’s core apps throughout iOS 27. Safari will organize tabs into topics, monitor webpages for changes and even build extensions from natural-language descriptions. Photos is set to gain a new Spatial Reframing edit tools including an upgraded Clean Up feature. Messages, Mail, and Calendar will be able to understand context, suggest actions and create events from simple descriptions.

## New features coming to apps in iOS 27

iOS 27 brings a mix of major Apple Intelligence upgrades and smaller quality-of-life improvements across Safari, Photos, Messages, AirPods, Passwords, Wallet, and other core iPhone apps. Apple is also making iOS more adaptable to different screen sizes and orientations, which are changes necessary for the [iPhone Duo](https://www.macworld.com/article/3230936/iphone-duo-the-five-most-important-things-you-need-to-know.html).

### Safari

Safari can automatically group open tabs into topics, making related pages easier to find. A new Notify Me feature will monitor webpages and alert you to changes such as price drops or products coming back into stock.  
There’s also a new Describe an Extension feature which lets users create custom Safari extensions simply by explaining what they want the extension to do.

![safari notify me logo](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/safari-notify-me-logo.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

### Photos

Photos gains significantly more powerful [AI editing tools](https://www.macworld.com/article/3194029/i-pushed-ios-27s-ai-photo-editing-tools-to-the-limit.html).

Reframe can alter the composition and perspective of an existing photo, while Extend generates new image content beyond the original frame when straightening a horizon or changing the aspect ratio.

![iOS 27 Image Editing](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/iOS-27-Image-editing.jpg?quality=50&strip=all)

Apple

Clean Up has also been improved, with Fast and High Quality modes for removing unwanted objects or details. High Quality mode can produce considerably more natural results, although more ambitious edits can still introduce distortions or invented details.

Photos also adds new categories and the [ability to save a frame from a video](https://www.macworld.com/article/3211750/how-to-save-a-video-frame-as-a-high-res-image-in-ios-27.html) as a full-resolution photo. The resulting HEIF or JPG retains the video’s original resolution, date, and location metadata rather than simply creating a screenshot.

### Camera

iOS 27 features a new more customizable camera interface that lets you pin the controls you use most often. For the iPhone 18 Pro, there are also “pro controls” like white balance, shutter speed, and manufal focus along with [Apple Reference Image](https://www.macworld.com/article/3210722/what-is-up-with-this-apple-reference-image-rumor.html), an authentication system designed to prove that a photo or video was genuinely captured on an iPhone and has not subsequently been manipulated.

The new Siri mode in the Camera app is a more convenient and logical way to access the Visual Intelligence features that used to require either a long-press of the camera button or a Control Center button.

### Messages

![iPhone shortcut to auto reply to messages using AI](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iPhone-shortcut-to-auto-reply-to-messages-using-AI.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

Messages gets several useful improvements.

You can [decide what the microphone button beside the text field does](https://www.macworld.com/article/3202129/ios-27-finally-lets-you-hide-the-audio-button-in-messages-heres-how.html). Under *Settings* > *Apps* > *Messages* > *Show in Text Field*, it can be set to Record Audio, Start Dictation, or None. Disabling it does not remove either feature: dictation remains available from the keyboard and audio messages remain in the + menu.

Voice-message playback controls are easier to access, while Apple Intelligence can suggest actions based on a conversation, such as creating a reminder, making a note, or finding relevant photos.

Messages will also gain smarter suggested replies that can better reflect the user’s writing style.

### Drawing

![Drawing app how to steps](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/drawing-app-how-to-steps.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

A [new dedicated Drawing app](https://www.macworld.com/article/3215130/ios-27-has-an-intriguing-new-drawing-app-for-scribbling-messages.html) replaces the old hidden handwriting interface. Accessible from the + menu, it uses the familiar pens, colours and drawing controls found in Notes and Markup, with finished drawings sent as images.

### Mail

Mail gains more context-aware smart replies, including responses that can better match the user’s usual writing style.

Apple Intelligence can also surface information from Mail elsewhere in iOS. For example, the Phone app could retrieve a flight confirmation number from an email when you call an airline.

### Phone

A new Call Context feature can surface information that may be useful when while on a call. Apple says the information is selected according to who you are calling rather than by listening to the conversation. For example, calling an airline could cause iOS to surface the relevant flight confirmation from Mail.

Birthday reminders can also appear when calling contacts whose birthdays are stored on the iPhone.

### FaceTime

FaceTime gains Dual Capture, allowing the front and rear cameras to be used at the same time during a call.

### Passwords

![passwords in ios 27 automatically fixing compromised passwords](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/passwords-ios-27-auto-fix.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Passwords in iOS 27 will fix things for you.

Apple

The Passwords app will continue to warn about weak, reused and compromised credentials, but iOS 27 goes a step further by offering to fix some of them automatically.

Using Apple Intelligence, Passwords can visit supported websites, change a vulnerable password and save the replacement credentials. See: [Apple got rid of my biggest password headache](https://www.macworld.com/article/3160935/apple-finally-got-rid-of-my-biggest-password-headache.html).

The usefulness of the feature will depend on how widely websites are supported and how well it handles obstacles such as two-factor authentication and unusual account-management interfaces.

### Shortcuts

Shortcuts gains Describe a Shortcut, allowing users to create automations simply by explaining what they want to happen.

Apple Intelligence will interpret the request and assemble the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually.

### Calendar

Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions.

Apple says the app can recognize contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually.

Siri can also create complete Calendar entries for information that is on your screen in that moment, or by taking a picture with the Siri mode in the Camera app.

### Image Playground

Image Playground is considerably more powerful and realistic.

Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized, or repositioned.

AI-generated images will include a SynthID watermark identifying them as synthetic content.

### Wallet

Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes.

Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch.

### Weather

Weather gets a clearer, more detailed forecast interface, with rearranged information tiles and new 10-day views showing precipitation probability/amount and wind speed throughout each day.

### Home app

Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy.

### Maps

Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models.

Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees.

### Podcasts

Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it.

### Fitness

Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share.

Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts.

## iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone

### CarPlay

CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content.

### AirPods

iOS 27 introduces several [new AirPods features](https://www.macworld.com/article/3220517/airpods-here-are-the-new-features-in-ios-27.html).

A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under *Settings* > *AirPods* > *Audio and Routing* > *Equalizer* > *Custom*.

Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate.

Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware.

Read [How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27](https://www.macworld.com/article/3207287/how-to-tune-your-airpods-with-a-custom-eq-in-ios-27.html).

## Other changes coming with iOS 27

It’s not only individual apps that are seeing changes.

### Home Screen and landscape mode

Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes.

More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather, and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen supports extra-large widgets.

These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they’re also well suited to Apple’s folding iPhone Duo.

iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape.

### Liquid Glass refinements

![Apple OS](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Apple-OS-27.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish.

### Ringtones, alarms and alert volume

iOS 27 finally [separates several sound-volume controls](https://www.macworld.com/article/3219137/finally-ios-27-lets-you-separately-adjust-the-volume-of-ringtones-alarms-and-alerts.html).

Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust:

* Ringtones
* Alarms and timers
* Alerts and system sounds

The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls.

Media and call volume continue to work independently as before.

### Keyboard

iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard.

It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster.

Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps.

### Privacy and Find My

iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared.

### Recovery and troubleshooting

Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device.

## System changes and how iOS 27 will make your iPhone faster

Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to [make iPhones faster](https://www.macworld.com/article/3160623/apple-finally-figured-out-how-to-make-old-iphones-faster.html), smoother and more efficient.

Apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.

The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.

[Our testing](https://www.macworld.com/article/3185415/ios-27-will-actually-speed-up-your-old-iphone-heres-the-proof.html) of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds.

Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance.

More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability.

That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets, and Liquid Glass refinements.

## Child safety and parental controls

![Screentime](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-time-27.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

There are lots of improvements coming to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainment, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week.

This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission.

**Ask to Browse**: Ask to Browse will expand the current Ask to Buy feature to the web. Apple says children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving.

**Communication Safety**: Communication Safety will continue to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos.

**Time Allowances and schedules**: Parents will be able to set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days.

**Redesigned Screen Time**: Screen Time will get a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment.

**Child accounts and family safety**: Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings.

Apple says it is working with the American Academy of Pediatrics to adapt its Family Media Plan.

## Accessibility changes coming in iOS 27

Accessibility features are smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27:

* VoiceOver gives richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content.
* Live Recognition lets users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses.
* Voice Control is more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact coordinate labels or numbers.
* Accessibility Reader will be able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation.

## iOS 27 compatibility

![iPhone 11](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/iphone-11.jpg?quality=50&strip=all)

iPhone 11 is supported by iOS 27.

Roman Loyola/IDG

According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware.

Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI requires an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, or iPhone 18 Pro. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM.

There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support.

However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to [how long Apple supports iPhones](https://www.macworld.com/article/675021/how-long-does-apple-support-iphones.html), the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s [Vintage iPhone list](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/102772).

The iOS 27 compatibility list is:

* [iPhone 17e](https://www.macworld.com/article/3097961/iphone-17e-review.html) (launched in **2026**)
* [iPhone 17](https://www.macworld.com/article/2925527/iphone-17-review.html), [17 Pro / 17 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/2921479/iphone-17-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2025**)
* [iPhone Air](https://www.macworld.com/article/2926985/iphone-air-review-a-whole-lot-less-for-a-whole-lot-more.html) (launched in **2025**)
* [iPhone 16e](https://www.macworld.com/article/2630661/iphone-16e-review.html) (launched in **2025**)
* [iPhone 16 / 16 Plus](https://www.macworld.com/article/2470661/iphone-16-and-16-plus-review.html) and [iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/2469098/iphone-16-pro-and-iphone-16-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2024**)
* [iPhone 15](https://www.macworld.com/article/2247687/iphone-15-review.html) / [15 Plus](https://www.macworld.com/article/2104222/iphone-15-plus-review.html) and [iPhone 15 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/2091512/iphone-15-pro-review.html) / [15 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/2081235/iphone-15-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2023**)
* [iPhone 14](https://www.macworld.com/article/1073091/iphone-14-review.html) / [14 Plus](https://www.macworld.com/article/1656045/iphone-14-plus-review-2.html) / [14 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/1070324/iphone-14-pro-review.html) / [14 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/1070386/iphone-14-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2022**)
* [iPhone SE 3](https://www.macworld.com/article/624052/iphone-se-2022-review.html) (launched in **2022**)
* [iPhone 13](https://www.macworld.com/article/544579/iphone-13-review.html) / [13 mini](https://www.macworld.com/article/668144/iphone-13-mini-review-last-of-a-dying-breed.html) / [13 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/450981/iphone-13-pro-review.html) / [13 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/538937/iphone-13-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2021**)
* [iPhone 12](https://www.macworld.com/article/234703/iphone-12-review.html) / [12 mini](https://www.macworld.com/article/234921/iphone-12-mini-review-a-concentration-not-a-reduction.html) / [12 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/668053/iphone-12-pro-review.html) / [12 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/668065/iphone-12-pro-max-review-2.html) (launched in **2020**)

The main dividing line for Apple Intelligence remains the iPhone 15 Pro generation: the standard iPhone 15 and all older models can run iOS 27, but they do not support Apple Intelligence.

## FAQ

---

1.

### When was iOS 27 released?

iOS 27 was releases around 10am Pacific Time on September 14, 2026.

2.

### Which iPhones get iOS 27?

The iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2 and newer get iOS 27. However, Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features requires iPhone 15 Pro or newer, and the new more expressive Siri voices feature requires iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, or newer.

3.

### Which iPhones will get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence in iOS 27?

The only iPhones that can run Siri AI are the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max and any newer generation. If you have a standard iPhone 15 then you won’t get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

entries.title: iOS 27 and macOS 27 are loaded with security fixes–here’s why
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

It used to be that operating system “point releases”—the minor updates throughout the year—contained around a dozen security vulnerability fixes. But that number has been growing in the last couple of years and has exploded in the past few months.

There were 35 security vulnerabilities fixed in iOS 26.0. That was up to 43 in iOS 26.5. A 26.5.2 update solely for security fixes added another 29 and iOS 26.6.7 [adds 79 more](https://support.apple.com/en-us/149041).

But that’s nothing compared to the latest round of updates. There are an unprecedented *122 security vulnerabilities fixed* in [iOS 27](https://support.apple.com/en-us/149034). Think that’s a lot? The macOS 27 update has [204 fixes listed on Apple’s Security Updates page](https://support.apple.com/en-us/149035). Even [watchOS 27](https://support.apple.com/en-us/149037) adds about 90 fixes.

Thanks to AI coding agents, this is the new normal. You can expect dozens of security vulnerabilities to be fixed every couple of months, at least for a while.

## Why is this happening?

You can thank, and blame, AI for this.

AI coding agents have gotten good. Very good. Not only has “vibe coding” become commonplace, but the best AI models can analyze and test very large code blocks and databases. And they find things that people miss.

A few months ago, we wrote about [Project Glasswing](https://www.macworld.com/article/3122026/how-ai-is-working-to-make-your-iphone-nearly-impervious-to-attacks.html), a collaboration between Anthropic and a handful of other companies (including Apple) to provide those companies’ security researchers with access to the company’s most advanced AI model, in the hopes of finding vulnerabilities before the models become public and all the bad actors get their hands on them.

The world we live in right now is one of security acceleration. Hackers and malicious groups can use advanced AI tools to find unique vulnerabilities that can, sometimes in combination with each other, compromise systems like never before. The sort of resources and research once only available to nation-states and the largest tech corporations are now broadly available.

But AI is having just as much of an impact on the positive side. Security researchers are using these tools to find more vulnerabilities than ever, reporting them to software companies, who now, thanks to AI coding tools, have the scope to address more of them more quickly.

For the time being, we’re in an AI-accelerated arms race between the hackers who use AI to find vulnerabilities and exploit them, and the researchers and developers who use AI to find vulnerabilities and fix or report them. And it’s resulting in increasingly large and important security update releases.

This may eventually wind down, as the AI coding tools get sophisticated and commonplace enough to more thoroughly test massive code databases and all their interactions with other code before its ever released. But for the time being, and likely for some time to come, expect operating system updates—including Apple’s—to fix a big list of security issues with every release.

entries.title: China Calls Amodei’s AI Proposal a New Cold War Playbook
entries.content:
## China rejects Amodei’s AI slowdown proposal, calling it fearmongering and a US attempt to contain China’s technology sector.

The debate over whether the world should slow down the development of advanced AI has quickly turned into something bigger than a technology argument. Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, [has called for a slower pace](https://securityaffairs.com/198994/ai/anthropic-ceo-calls-for-an-ai-slowdown-is-it-possible.html) of development, arguing that AI capabilities are advancing faster than our ability to understand and control them. His proposal has now run straight into the geopolitical reality of the US-China competition.

In his essay, *“[We Must Pace the Frontier](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier)“*, Amodei argues that the industry needs more time to build effective safeguards around increasingly capable AI systems. He isn’t calling for an end to AI development. His argument is that capability gains should slow enough to give safety research, testing and oversight a chance to catch up.

One of his main concerns is the growing ability of AI agents to act on their own. Amodei warns that a large number of increasingly capable agents could, within six to twelve months, become capable of carrying out complex operations across the internet and potentially cause enormous damage if they aren’t properly controlled. The warning follows recent incidents in which AI systems have already been used to perform cyber operations with a level of autonomy that would have been difficult to imagine only a few years ago.

Amodei’s proposal has three main elements: stronger independent testing of advanced models, greater coordination between leading AI companies, and international cooperation on safety. Anthropic says it is prepared to give independent evaluators permanent, employee-level access to its systems so they can assess safety measures and investigate incidents.

The difficult part starts when China enters the discussion.

Amodei argues that the United States needs to maintain its lead in advanced AI and supports continuing restrictions on China’s access to the most advanced AI chips and chipmaking equipment. He says a Chinese lead in frontier AI could create serious risks for the United States and the wider world.

The Government of Beijing strongly disagrees with that framing. China’s Foreign Ministry accused Amodei of spreading fear and argued that confrontation and competition would damage international efforts to establish rules for AI. China’s state-backed *Global Times* went further, describing the proposal as a “Cold War playbook” aimed at containing China’s technology sector.

Chinese officials are also warning about AI, but from the opposite direction. Chen Yixin, head of China’s Ministry of State Security, recently warned that advanced AI could be used by hostile actors to discover vulnerabilities at scale, conduct complex hacking operations and steal sensitive information.

*“In an essay posted Sunday on social media, Chen Yixin, head of China’s Ministry of State Security, warned that, in the hands of “hostile forces and individuals with ulterior motives,” this technology could pose a direct threat to “our political, institutional, and ideological security.”” The Associated Press [reports](https://apnews.com/article/china-anthropic-ai-us-amodei-3da458d2c078da3e60900728d59f1ae8).*

*“Citing the capabilities of powerful technologies from U.S. companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, Chen warned that “certain nations and organizations” now have the capabilities to “rapidly discover vulnerabilities at scale … and execute complex hacking tasks.” That, he wrote, poses “serious risks to my country’s critical information infrastructure.””*

That contrast is important. Both sides are talking about AI security, but they don’t agree on what the security problem actually is.

Washington is concerned that China could gain access to capabilities that strengthen its military, intelligence and cyber operations. Beijing sees US restrictions on chips and AI technology as an attempt to prevent China from closing the technological gap.

The recent dispute over AI model distillation has made the situation even more complicated. US agencies have accused Chinese AI developers of aggressively extracting capabilities from leading American models, including Claude and GPT. Beijing has rejected those allegations and argued that model distillation is a common technique used across the AI industry.

This creates a problem for any proposal based on international cooperation. How do you persuade two countries to slow down together when each side believes that slowing down alone could leave it at a strategic disadvantage?

President rejected calls to slow AI development, despite warnings from leading tech executives and Democrats about existential risks. Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Elon Musk urged a more cautious approach, but Trump said the US must maintain its global AI leadership while allowing some safeguards.

*“Look, we’re leading China in AI . . . and, frankly, I want to keep it that way, because whoever wins AI, wins,” Trump told reporters during a trip to his Doonbeg golf course in Ireland, [Financial Times reported](https://www.ft.com/content/cae60732-f929-4735-a627-db8c14e7c7ed?syn-25a6b1a6=1).  “We can put guardrails, we can do this and that, but I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn’t be bringing it up and they’re bringing up things that won’t happen,” he added.*

That puts Amodei’s proposal in a difficult position. The companies developing the most advanced models are increasingly warning that safety needs more time, while the political leadership in Washington sees AI leadership as a strategic asset that cannot be surrendered. Sam Altman and Elon Musk have backed Amodei’s call for greater caution, and other major AI leaders have also moved toward stronger safety measures.

The timing is particularly interesting because Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are expected to discuss AI governance at their planned September 24 meeting. Any agreement between Washington and Beijing would have to deal with two very different priorities: controlling the risks created by increasingly autonomous AI systems while making sure neither side believes it is giving the other a technological advantage.

For cybersecurity professionals, this is more than a political dispute. The capabilities being discussed are already relevant to vulnerability discovery, exploitation, credential theft, surveillance and large-scale automated operations. The question is no longer simply how powerful AI models can become, but how quickly that power can be turned into real-world action.

That’s where the debate over slowing AI becomes particularly difficult. You can slow the development of a model, but you can’t easily slow a global competition in which governments, companies and attackers all have strong incentives to keep moving.

And that’s probably the uncomfortable part of the discussion: the countries most capable of creating the rules are also the countries with the strongest reasons not to slow down.

entries.title: Reward AI 发布了机器人基础模型 OM-1，核心卖点是：只从人类操作数据中学习，不需要遥操作，不需要机器人专属数据，训练完直接部署到桌面机械臂、工业机械臂、人形机器人上，不用针对每种机器人做微...
entries.content:
Reward AI 发布了机器人基础模型 OM-1，核心卖点是：只从人类操作数据中学习，不需要遥操作，不需要机器人专属数据，训练完直接部署到桌面机械臂、工业机械臂、人形机器人上，不用针对每种机器人做微调。  
  
Reward AI 脱胎于斯坦福大学的 DexCap 项目。DexCap 是一套便携式人手动作捕捉系统，能记录人在日常操作中手指的精细动作。OM-1 在此基础上更进一步，设计了一套叫 Omnibody Hand 的 7 自由度可穿戴设备，让人戴着它正常工作、做饭、整理东西，设备会同步采集视觉、触觉、力度等多模态数据。换句话说，人照常干活，数据自动录好，机器人直接从这些数据里学会怎么操控物体。  
  
这条路线和当前主流做法不一样。大多数机器人基础模型（比如 Physical Intelligence 的 π0、Figure AI 的 Helix）依赖大量遥操作数据，需要人远程控制机器人做示范，再从示范中学习。遥操作数据采集成本高、效率低，而且跟具体机器人硬件绑定。OM-1 绕开了这个瓶颈，直接从人手动作学习，数据采集更快，理论上也更容易规模化。  
  
从演示视频看，OM-1 能完成手机包装（四臂协作）、调酒、叠衣服、拔网线这类任务，都是实时速度，没有加速。拔网线这个任务看着简单，其实需要精确按压卡扣才能拔出来，属于精细操作。官方称学会一个全新任务只需不到 30 分钟的人类演示数据。  
  
OM-1 还展现了一些自发行为：多臂协作时一只臂会自动补偿另一只臂的失误，遇到外部干扰会重试，环境变化太大时会主动停下。  
  
目前 OM-1 处于研发展示阶段，Reward AI 没有公布商业化时间表和定价。对于机器人行业来说，如果"从人类数据直接学习"这条路能跑通并规模化，将大幅降低机器人技能训练的门槛，让新机器人硬件一出厂就能继承已有的操作能力，而不用从头采集训练数据。

![Reward AI](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/2097043403888586752/cRohJUYD_normal.jpg)

Reward AI@RewardAI\_

Introducing OM-1, our first robot foundation model, zero-shot generalizing to any robot: table-top arms, industrial arms and humanoids.  
- learned directly from human manipulation data  
- no teleop/robot data  
- close to human-level dexterity and efficiency  
- multi-robot collab

entries.title: Greg Brockman on the defenders' window that closes when frontier AI capabilities become distributed:...
entries.content:
Greg Brockman on the defenders' window that closes when frontier AI capabilities become distributed:  
  
"Hugging Face shows... what future capabilities will be like when they are broadly diffused and in the hands of threat actors. And that will happen."  
  
"In the case of Hugging Face, you saw both an AI that was able to hack out of a secure environment and hack into a company's production environment."  
  
"This capability broadly diffused is something that will really empower threat actors in new ways. Defenders need to use this time before that technology's broadly available to secure themselves. The nice thing about it is it's dual-use."  
  
"If you can find vulnerabilities, if you're an attacker, you can use it for no good, but if you're a defender, you can patch. If you're a defender, you control the battleground. You control the setup of your systems."  
  
"Our belief right now is that there's this window... You need to move, use these frontier capabilities that you will have differential access to... and you can use that to move yourself up so that as the frontier capabilities get better, you get pulled along too."

entries.title: Manage end-user OAuth consent for AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entries.content:
AI agents often need to access services such as GitHub and Slack on a user’s behalf. Before an agent can act, the user must authenticate with the provider and explicitly approve the requested access. The application must then securely associate the resulting OAuth grant with the user who authorized it. This process is called session binding.

Previously, customers using the AgentCore Identity (a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore) three-legged OAuth (3LO) flow (also known as OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow) had to build and host their own session binding infrastructure. This included presenting the authorization URL, hosting a public HTTPS callback, authenticating the returning user, managing browser sessions, and calling `CompleteResourceTokenAuth` to complete the flow.

AgentCore Identity now offers a Consent portal, a managed web experience and session binding endpoint for AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You create a portal for a gateway and share its URL with your users. Users authenticate with your organization’s identity provider (IdP), review the services available to the agent, and grant consent to individual providers. The portal handles the browser redirects and session binding, while AgentCore Identity stores the resulting tokens in its token vault.

This capability is particularly useful for agents accessed through IDE and Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients such as Kiro, Claude Code, Cursor, and Visual Studio Code. Users can grant consent before invoking a tool, and subsequent tool calls can use the token already stored for that user. In this post, we use a software development assistant as an example. We walk through the administrator and end-user experiences on the AWS Management Console and browser, and show how to review the resulting activity in AWS CloudTrail.

[![Consent portal architecture: users authenticate with the corporate IdP and per-user tokens are stored in AgentCore Identity](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-1.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-1.png)

Figure 1: The Consent portal authenticates the user with the corporate IdP, uses its IAM execution role to discover configured gateway targets, presents provider connections, completes session binding, and stores per-user tokens in the AgentCore Identity token vault

## Example scenario: Give a development assistant access to GitHub

Consider a company named Example Corp that provides its developers with an AI coding assistant through an AgentCore Gateway. The assistant has two targets:

* A GitHub target that can list repositories and create issues.
* A Slack target that can list public channels and post messages.

Example Corp uses its corporate IdP to authenticate employees. The administrator wants each GitHub and Slack OAuth grant to remain associated with the employee who approved it. Developers can connect either provider independently and return to their IDE without repeated prompts.

The walkthrough follows these two roles:

* **Administrator:** Configures the corporate IdP, GitHub and Slack gateway targets, execution role, and Consent portal, and then sends the portal URL to developers.
* **End user:** Opens the URL, signs in with the corporate IdP, connects GitHub when needed, and can grant Slack access separately.

## Prerequisites

Before starting the walkthrough, Example Corp needs:

* An [AWS account with access to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/agentcore-get-started-cli.html).
* An [AgentCore Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-quick-start.html) configured with [JWT inbound authorization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-inbound-auth.html).
* An IDE or MCP client configured to connect to the same AgentCore Gateway that will be attached to the Consent portal.
* Administrative access to the corporate IdP.
* A registered [GitHub OAuth App](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/creating-an-oauth-app) and [Slack app](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth/) for a development or test workspace.
* Permission to register the AgentCore Identity callback URL in each provider application.

## Getting started

The following steps show what the Example Corp administrator configures and what a developer experiences after receiving the portal URL.

#### Steps for administrator

The administrator completes Steps 1–6 to configure the identity provider, gateway targets, execution role, and Consent portal.

#### Step 1: Prepare the corporate IdP and gateway connections

**Administrator IAM policy**

Attach this policy to the administrator identity that performs Steps 1–3. Replace the account ID.

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ManageConsentPortalResources",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "bedrock-agentcore:CreateConsentPortal",
        "bedrock-agentcore:GetConsentPortal",
        "bedrock-agentcore:ListConsentPortals",
        "bedrock-agentcore:CreateOauth2CredentialProvider",
        "bedrock-agentcore:GetOauth2CredentialProvider",
        "bedrock-agentcore:ListOauth2CredentialProviders",
        "bedrock-agentcore:GetGateway",
        "bedrock-agentcore:ListGateways",
        "bedrock-agentcore:CreateGatewayTarget",
        "bedrock-agentcore:GetGatewayTarget",
        "bedrock-agentcore:ListGatewayTargets",
        "bedrock-agentcore:UpdateGatewayTarget"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "CreateAndPassExecutionRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "iam:CreateRole",
        "iam:GetRole",
        "iam:PutRolePolicy",
        "iam:GetRolePolicy",
        "iam:PassRole"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/service-role/AmazonBedrockAgentCoreConsentPortal*"
    }
  ]
}
```

The AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) statement covers the **Create default role** option on the console, which creates a service role named `AmazonBedrockAgentCoreConsentPortalDefaultServiceRole-<suffix>`. If you supply your own role instead, scope `iam:PassRole` to that role ARN.

#### Step 2: Configure the corporate IdP application

1. In the corporate IdP, create an OpenID Connect (OIDC) web application for the Consent portal.
2. Enable the authorization code grant and generate a client ID and client secret.
3. Configure the login scopes, at minimum `openid`.
4. Record the OpenID Connect (OIDC) discovery URL. The portal uses the authorization endpoint, token endpoint, and signing keys from this document.
5. Add a temporary callback URL. You replace it in Step 6, after the portal URL exists.

The IdP must issue a JSON Web Token (JWT) access token that the portal can validate. For example, with Okta, use a custom authorization server with an access policy that permits the application and the authorization code grant. With Auth0, configure an audience when needed so the IdP returns a signed JWT access token instead of an opaque token.

#### Step 3: Create the IdP credential provider

The portal reads the IdP client ID and client secret from an OAuth2 credential provider.

1. Open the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore console.
2. Under **Build**, choose **Identity**.
3. In **Outbound Auth**, choose **Add Outbound Auth**, and then choose **Add OAuth client**.
4. Enter a name, such as `gateway-demo-idp`.
5. Enter the client ID and client secret from the corporate IdP application, and provide the OIDC discovery configuration.
6. Choose **Add OAuth client**.

[![AgentCore Identity page showing one sign-in credential provider and separate GitHub and Slack outbound providers](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-5.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-5.png)

Figure 2: AgentCore Identity uses one credential provider for portal sign-in and separate outbound providers for GitHub and Slack

#### Step 4: Verify outbound prerequisites

Before creating the Consent portal, confirm:

* The GitHub and Slack OAuth applications are registered, and their client secrets are stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
* AgentCore Identity has separate outbound OAuth credential providers for GitHub and Slack, and each generated callback URL is registered with the matching provider application.
* The GitHub and Slack gateway targets use the authorization code grant, request only the required scopes, and have a **Ready** status.
* The Consent portal execution role selected in Step 5 can read any customer-managed secrets referenced by the outbound credential providers.

After the portal URL is assigned, configure each target’s default return URL in Step 6.

[![Gateway with independent GitHub and Slack targets, each linked to its own outbound OAuth provider](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-6.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-6.png)

Figure 3: The gateway exposes independent GitHub and Slack targets, each associated with its own outbound OAuth provider

#### Step 5: Create the Consent portal

On the **Identity** page, the **Consent portals** section lists the portals in the account and AWS Region.

[![Consent portals section on the AgentCore Identity page listing portals in the account and Region](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-2.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-2.png)

Figure 4: The Consent portals section on the AgentCore Identity page. Create a portal only when a gateway uses 3LO that requires user consent

1. In **Consent portals**, choose **Create portal**.
2. Under **Consent portal details**, for **Name**, enter a name such as `consent-portal-heqk0`. Names accept 1–50 characters, using letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
3. Optionally enter a **Description** of up to 512 characters.
4. For **Gateway**, select the development assistant’s gateway. The gateway name is visible to end users in the Consent portal, so choose a clear, recognizable name. One Consent portal is allowed per gateway, and the gateway can’t be changed after creation.
5. Under **IdP credential configurations**, for **IdP Credential Provider**, select the OAuth2 credential provider created in Step 3.
6. Under **Scopes**, keep the required `openid` scope. Additional scopes are optional. Choose **Add scope** only when your IdP or application requires them.
7. For **Audience – optional**, keep **None** unless your gateway specifies audiences. The value is validated against the audiences configured on the AgentCore Gateway.
8. Expand **Permissions**. For **IAM permissions**, choose **Create default role** to have the console create a service role with the required permissions, or choose **Use another role** to select an existing role.
9. Choose **Create portal**.

[![Consent portal detail page showing Creating status with the portal ARN and execution role but no URL yet](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-3.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-3.png)

Figure 5: While the status is Creating, the portal ARN and execution role are visible but the URL isn’t assigned yet

When provisioning finishes, the status changes to **Active**, the **Consent portal URL** appears, and a **Launch Consent portal** button opens it in a new tab. The URL follows the pattern `https://<gateway-name>.consent-portal.bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com`.

[![Consent portal detail page showing Active status with the assigned portal URL](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-4.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-4.png)

Figure 6: After the portal becomes Active, the console shows the assigned URL that you share with end users

#### Step 6: Register callback URLs and send the portal URL

1. Copy the **consent portal URL** from the portal details page.
2. In the corporate IdP application, for example, Amazon Cognito, Okta, or Auth0, replace the temporary callback with `<portal-url>/callback`. Don’t add a trailing slash. This isn’t the GitHub or Slack application callback. Those applications use the unique AgentCore Identity `callbackUrl`.
3. For each 3LO gateway target, set the default return URL to `<portal-url>/connect/callback`.
4. Confirm that each outbound provider application contains the AgentCore Identity callback URL returned when its OAuth credential provider was created.
5. Test the portal URL in a browser.
6. Send the portal URL to the development team through an approved communication channel.

#### Callback URL reference

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **URL** | **Where it is configured** | **Purpose** |
| `<portal-url>/callback` | Corporate IdP application | Returns the user after portal login |
| `<portal-url>/connect/callback` | Gateway target as the default return URL | Returns the user to the managed session binding endpoint |
| AgentCore Identity `callbackUrl` | Outbound provider application | Sends the provider’s authorization code to AgentCore Identity |

After completing the provider callbacks and gateway targets, verify the final administrator configuration before sharing the portal URL.

#### Steps for end user

The end user completes Step 7 to sign in and connect providers after receiving the portal URL.

#### Step 7: Sign in and connect providers

1. Open the portal URL in a browser.
2. Choose **Sign in**. The browser redirects to the Example Corp IdP.
3. Authenticate with the corporate identity. The portal then uses its IAM execution role to retrieve the gateway’s configured targets and their connection state.
4. On the **Connections** page, review the GitHub and Slack OAuth clients and their target status.
5. Choose **Connect** for GitHub.
6. Review the scopes on GitHub’s consent page and approve access.
7. After the browser returns to the portal, verify that GitHub shows **Connected** while Slack remains **Not connected**. This demonstrates that grants are independent for each provider.
8. If the agent needs Slack, choose **Connect** for Slack, select the workspace, review the requested permissions, and approve the app. Otherwise, leave Slack unconnected until it is needed.
9. Return to the IDE or MCP client configured to use the same AgentCore Gateway attached to the Consent portal, and retry the applicable GitHub or Slack tool call through that gateway.

The following screenshots capture useful checkpoints for the walkthrough.

[![Consent portal Connections page showing GitHub OAuth client and target as Not connected](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-7.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-7.png)

Figure 7: The Consent portal discovers the GitHub OAuth client and its target. Both remain Not connected until the user grants access

[![GitHub authorization page showing the scopes and organization access requested by the OAuth app](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-8.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-8.png)

Figure 8: GitHub displays the scopes and organization access requested by the OAuth application before the user authorizes it

[![Consent portal showing the GitHub OAuth client and target as Connected after session binding](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-9.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-9.png)

Figure 9: After GitHub returns the authorization result, the portal completes session binding and shows the OAuth client and target as Connected

[![Consent portal showing GitHub Connected and Slack Not connected](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-10.png)](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/09/14/ML-21874-10.png)

Figure 10: GitHub remains Connected while Slack is Not connected, demonstrating that users grant consent independently for each outbound provider

## Behind the scenes

1. The portal validates the IdP response and establishes an encrypted browser session.
2. The portal uses its execution role to list the attached gateway’s 3LO targets.
3. When the user chooses **Connect**, the portal calls `GetResourceOauth2Token` and receives an authorization URL and session URI.
4. After the provider returns the authorization code to AgentCore Identity, the browser returns to the portal’s managed session binding endpoint.
5. The portal calls `CompleteResourceTokenAuth` with the authenticated user context.
6. When the provider returns a refresh token, AgentCore Identity stores it and automatically uses it to obtain a new access token after the current access token expires. Sometimes no valid refresh token is available, because the provider didn’t issue one or it has expired or been revoked. In that case, the user must return to the Consent portal and reauthorize when the access token can no longer be used. Configure the provider to issue refresh tokens where supported. For example, enable user-to-server token expiration for GitHub or token rotation for Slack.

The next time the developer opens the portal, connected providers remain visible. The developer doesn’t need to approve a provider again unless the grant is revoked, expires, or requires renewed consent. The developer can also choose **Disconnect** and later connect the provider again.

## Review consent activity in AWS CloudTrail

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore records consent operations in AWS CloudTrail. In **CloudTrail event history**, filter **Event source** by `bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com`, then review:

* `GetResourceOauth2Token` when the portal starts OAuth authorization for a provider.
* `CompleteResourceTokenAuth` when session binding is completed.
* `GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT` when the portal obtains gateway access for the authenticated user.

A `GetResourceOauth2Token` event identifies the credential provider, requested scopes, OAuth flow, portal execution role, and Region. Sensitive token and state values are redacted.

```
{
  "eventSource": "bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com",
  "eventName": "GetResourceOauth2Token",
  "awsRegion": "ap-southeast-2",
  "userIdentity": {
    "type": "AssumedRole",
    "arn": "arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/AmazonBedrockAgentCoreConsentPortalDefaultServiceRole-example/consent-dashboard-example"
  },
  "requestParameters": {
    "workloadIdentityToken": "HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS",
    "resourceCredentialProviderName": "gateway-demo-github",
    "scopes": ["read:user", "repo"],
    "oauth2Flow": "USER_FEDERATION",
    "customState": "HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS"
  },
  "resources": [
    {
      "accountId": "111122223333",
      "type": "AWS::BedrockAgentCore::OAuth2CredentialProvider",
      "ARN": "arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:ap-southeast-2:111122223333:token-vault/default/oauth2credentialprovider/gateway-demo-github"
    }
  ],
  "managementEvent": true
}
```

For failures, use `errorCode` and `errorMessage` with the event time, assumed role, Region, credential provider, and requested scopes to identify the cause.

## Clean up

When you no longer need the resources:

1. Open the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore console and delete the Consent portal.
2. Remove the portal callback URLs from the corporate IdP application and gateway targets.
3. Delete the gateway targets that reference the outbound credential providers.
4. Delete the outbound OAuth credential providers and corporate IdP credential provider if they aren’t used elsewhere.
5. Delete the portal execution role if no other resource uses it.

**Note:** Delete the gateway target before deleting its outbound credential provider. A credential provider still referenced by a target can’t be deleted.

## Conclusion

The Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Consent portal gives administrators a managed way to configure end-user OAuth consent for an AgentCore Gateway. Administrators connect the corporate IdP, execution role, gateway, and outbound providers, and then share one URL. End users authenticate, review available providers, and grant consent individually. The portal handles the browser flow and managed session binding, while AgentCore Identity protects the resulting user tokens in the token vault.

For end-to-end examples using Microsoft Entra ID and Okta, see the following Amazon Bedrock AgentCore samples on GitHub:

* [Consent portal with authorization code flow targets](https://github.com/awslabs/agentcore-samples/tree/main/01-features/05-authenticate-and-authorize/07-consent-portal-auth-code-flow-targets)
* [AgentCore Gateway target using the OAuth authorization code flow](https://github.com/awslabs/agentcore-samples/tree/main/01-features/07-centralize-and-govern-your-ai-infrastructure/01-gateway/01-attach-targets/mcp/mcp-servers/01-configure-auth/authorization-code-flow)

To learn more, see [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/)

entries.title: What blog posts influenced your thinking the most?
entries.content:
[My comment](https://lobste.rs/s/lbavmm/what_blog_posts_influenced_your_thinking#c_4fxnwn) on [What blog posts influenced your thinking the most?](https://lobste.rs/s/lbavmm/what_blog_posts_influenced_your_thinking) — Lobste.rs.

An early Joel Spolsky one for me was [The Law of Leaky Abstractions](https://www.joelonsoftware.com/2002/11/11/the-law-of-leaky-abstractions/). I read that near the start of my career and it's encouraged me to *always* be looking for improved understanding of the layers under where I'm working, just in case one of those abstractions leaks.

A more recent one, from 2018, is [Migrations: the sole scalable fix to tech debt](https://lethain.com/migrations/) by Will Larson. I absolutely love his idea that migrations (e.g. replacing one service with a new one, or switching database engines, or whatever) are part and parcel of software engineering and are a skill that you should invest in and get good at, not avoid or treat as special one-offs.

[The Engineer/Manager Pendulum](https://charity.wtf/p/the-engineer-manager-pendulum) by Charity Majors was hugely influential for me. I was stuck in engineering management and worried that if I switched back to being an "Individual Contributor" (ugh I hate that term) I'd damage my career. Charity gave me permission to make the switch by pointing out that many of the most successful software developers pendulum from one track to the other multiple times over their career, and doing so makes you better at both sides.

Tags: [joel-spolsky](https://simonwillison.net/tags/joel-spolsky), [software-engineering](https://simonwillison.net/tags/software-engineering), [will-larson](https://simonwillison.net/tags/will-larson), [charity-majors](https://simonwillison.net/tags/charity-majors)

entries.title: Yellowstone National Park retrieved 280 hats from hydrothermal vents this summer
entries.content:
[Yellowstone National Park](https://www.popsci.com/environment/yellowstone-summer-snow/) attracts more than 4.5 million visitors from around the world every year. [Many sightseers](https://www.popsci.com/environment/yellowstone-first-grizzly-bear-2026/) arrive well prepared to admire the [hotsprings, geysers](https://www.popsci.com/environment/new-yellowstone-geyser-biscuit-basin/), [scenic lookouts](https://www.popsci.com/environment/new-stamp-bison-yellowstone/), and [wildlife](https://www.popsci.com/environment/yellowstone-park-babies/), but there is only so much anyone can do about life’s little unexpected accidents. Each season, Yellowstone’s gusty winds are responsible for blowing away hundreds of hats, maps, and even sunglasses from the heads and hands of onlookers. And every season, park workers scour the grounds to gather up any lost items that landed far from the walkways and trails.

While the tally so far isn’t quite as large as [last year’s haul](https://www.popsci.com/environment/hats-recovered-yellowstone-park/), Yellowstone officials still impressively [retrieved more than 280 hats](https://www.usgs.gov/observatories/yvo/news/caps-trash-and-other-hydrothermal-funky-finds-2026-edition?fbclid=IwY2xjawUVGFBwZG9mBWV4dG4DYWVtAjEwAGJyaWQRMWFaemdJSWgzZUNGbUVzSW1zcnRjBmFwcF9pZBAyMjIwMzkxNzg4MjAwODkyAAEeruasOUeTy3mQN0t3t8TQrRUXLlJuz97mFp_kVKLU9aA0_1A7zvxErQCykWU_aem_1cMy1iyvoMYh3fdVf12lqw) from the hydrothermal areas. Workers cited standouts including a FIFA 2026 Men’s World Cup souvenir and a baseball cap ironically emblazoned with “Cowboy Hat.” But just because they aren’t suited for floating around roiling geysers doesn’t mean they’re destined for a landfill. Once the 2026 season draws to a close, all of the collected hats will be cleaned and donated to local clothing organizations.

![Table of random items retrieved from Yellowstone park including camera lens caps, pacifiers, hair ties, and sunglasses](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Yellowstone-Lost-Items.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

*Yellowstone officials recommend storing items deep in your pockets and always throwing litter into trash bins. Credit: Yellowstone National Park*

Caps are only one type of lost item located amid the hunts. Workers scooped up more than $18 in coins from around the world during the summer search. Canadian dollars, euros, pesos, and yen were scattered among the U.S. change, many apparently tossed into hot springs and geysers as if they were wishing wells. Yellowstone officials took the occasion to remind everyone that hydrothermal formations are not made to receive wished-upon coins. Not only will your dream remain unfulfilled—the foreign additions often introduce destructive algae and bacteria into the delicate ecosystems.

Other common detritus in the haul included plenty of paper and plastic trash, hair ties, hotel key cards, children’s toys, eyewear, and camera lens caps. Standout oddities such as AirPods, an inhaler, and even a single Uno card also made the list of finds.

![Particularly odd lost items including retainers, trading cards, golf tees, and AirPods](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Yellowstone-Toys.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

*A single Uno card was also among the fines. Credit: Yellowstone National Park*

As always, Yellowstone workers reminded everyone that the seasonal roundup also serves as an excellent reminder to “stash your trash.” Visitors are encouraged to place any litter or lightweight items deep in their pockets or bags until they reach a trash can. And although headwear is always important protection from the sun, people may want to consider temporarily removing their hats while trekking through especially windy areas of the park.

The post [Yellowstone National Park retrieved 280 hats from hydrothermal vents this summer](https://www.popsci.com/environment/yellowstone-national-park-lost-hats-summer-2026/) appeared first on [Popular Science](https://www.popsci.com).

entries.title: Apple standing its ground in Epic's App Store fee suit
entries.content:
The Supreme Court will begin hearing cases again in October, which is where Apple hopes to convince the court to throw out its injunction violation against Epic. Here are its arguments why.  
  

![Apple Park surrounded by trees at sunrise, forming a large ring structure with a glowing sun on the horizon and soft light illuminating the landscape](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/68983-145392-Apple-Park-sun-xl.jpg)  
Epic's lawsuit against Apple continues

  
Apple and Epic have been battling each other for [over six years](https://appleinsider.com/articles/20/08/23/apple-versus-epic-games-fortnite-app-store-saga——the-story-so-far) over how Apple operates the [App Store](https://appleinsider.com/inside/app-store "App Store") and charges commissions. The initial lawsuit ended in near total victory for Apple except for a provision about [anti-steering practices](https://appleinsider.com/articles/22/07/15/apple-argues-that-anti-steering-injunction-was-legally-improper-in-new-brief).  
  
The District Court found Apple [in violation](https://appleinsider.com/articles/25/04/30/fortnite-could-return-to-apple-app-store-after-judge-finds-apple-in-violation-of-injunction) of an injunction after it allegedly failed to provide a [competitive alternative](https://appleinsider.com/articles/24/01/16/apples-app-store-anti-steering-rules-are-gone-but-the-replacement-isnt-much-better) to anti-steering. Apple's latest filings [restate its arguments](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/05/21/after-failed-delays-apple-files-formal-request-with-supreme-court-to-review-epic-case) for the Supreme Court, suggesting the injunction violation was found in error and exceeded the District Court's limits.

entries.title: OpenAI stuck fighting Musk antitrust suit after Apple finds a way out
entries.content:
Elon Musk is seemingly done attacking Apple over its decision to integrate ChatGPT into iPhone features.

Back in 2024, when the partnership was first announced, [Musk slammed the integration](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2024/06/elon-musk-is-livid-about-new-openai-apple-deal/) as an agreement from Apple to let OpenAI install “creepy spyware” on users’ devices. The next year, [he sued](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2025/08/elon-musk-sues-apple-openai-to-block-exclusive-iphone-chatgpt-integration/), claiming the partnership gave the firms a “monopoly” on Apple users’ AI prompts, which allegedly harmed competition in both smartphone and chatbot markets.

For Musk, the fight with Apple seemingly escalated after he believed that his chatbot, [Grok, was perhaps being illegally blocked](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2025/08/apple-gets-yanked-into-elon-musks-chatbot-war-with-openai/) from topping Apple’s App Store rankings. Last August, he claimed that “Apple is behaving in a manner that makes it impossible for any AI company besides OpenAI to reach #1 in the App Store, which is an unequivocal antitrust violation.”

entries.title: Founder’s cost-cutting obsession drove Unitree lead in cheap humanoid robots
entries.content:
China leads the world in churning out humanoid robots and four-legged robot dogs that also happen to be the most affordable on the market—and Unitree Robotics’ founder Wang Xingxing is arguably one of the people most responsible for that Chinese lead.

The introverted founder, who prominently appeared at a 2025 business symposium hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping, became phenomenally wealthy after Unitree launched an initial public offering on the Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market on August 19. But extensive reporting by [Beijing-based Caijing Magazine](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=MjM5NDU5NTM4MQ==&mid=2653732248&idx=1&sn=796118fd794f591bcdeb383ef5d40f1d&chksm=bcc179fd92845a6e7b6ffad9354e21e66c150c331f2c84a4b2792098adfe48657f36c1276985&scene=0&xtrack=1) suggests Unitree’s success so far has been driven by Wang’s extreme micromanagement leadership style—an approach that may be more suited to a small startup than a fast-growing robotics company.

Caijing’s interviews with Unitree employees and investors paint a picture of Wang as someone who personally decides nearly every aspect of corporate strategy or product design, including the colors of materials and lengths of individual screws. The Caijing Magazine feature published on August 31, titled “The King of Unitree,” was [translated into English by ChinaTalk](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/the-king-of-unitree), a US-based think tank and media organization, on September 10.
